definition_en: the ability to bend easily or to change in order to suit new conditions
core_image: 舞者把身体弯成一道弧，肌肉仍然放松
scene: 瑜伽提高了她身体的柔韧性。 Yoga improved her flexibility.
sceneCN: 这里 flexibility 是「柔韧性」（第 1 个义项）；句意：瑜伽提高了她身体的柔韧性。

senses.title: Physical bend
senses.definition: the ability of the body or a material to bend without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 身体或材料弯曲而不断裂的能力
senses.example: Yoga improved her flexibility.
senses.exampleCN: 瑜伽提高了她的柔韧性。
senses.why: This is the literal sense of bending.
senses.whyCN: 这是弯曲的字面义项。

senses.title: Ability to change
senses.definition: the ability to change plans when conditions change
senses.definitionCN: 情况变化时改变计划的能力
senses.example: The job requires flexibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作需要灵活性。
senses.why: A mind or schedule that can bend is called flexible.
senses.whyCN: 能弯曲的头脑或日程被称为灵活。

senses.title: Adaptability
senses.definition: the quality of a system that can adjust to new uses
senses.definitionCN: 系统能适应新用途的性质
senses.example: The software offers great flexibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件提供很大的适应性。
senses.why: The bending metaphor extends to tools and systems.
senses.whyCN: 弯曲的隐喻扩展到工具与系统。

senses.title: Willingness to compromise
senses.definition: the willingness to change a position in a discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论中愿意改变立场的态度
senses.example: Both sides showed flexibility.
senses.exampleCN: 双方都表现出变通。
senses.why: A rigid position cannot bend toward agreement.
senses.whyCN: 僵硬的立场无法向共识弯曲。

intro.en: Flexibility comes from Latin flectere, to bend, through flexibilis and flexibilitas.
intro.cn: flexibility 源自拉丁语 flectere（弯曲），经 flexibilis 与 flexibilitas 而来。

items.en: Flectere meant to bend or turn.
items.cn: flectere 意为弯曲或转向。

items.en: Flexibilis meant that which can be bent.
items.cn: flexibilis 意为可被弯曲的。

items.en: Flexibilitas named the quality of bending.
items.cn: flexibilitas 指可弯曲的性质。

items.en: Flexibility named the bending of the body.
items.cn: flexibility 指身体的弯曲能力。

items.en: The word extended to plans, systems, and views.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到计划、系统和观点。

note.en: Flexibility is compared with similar-looking words and with words for adaptability.
note.cn: 把 flexibility 与形近词以及表示适应性的词作比较。

definition_en: the chemical element of atomic number 7, a colourless, odourless gas that makes up about four fifths of the air
core_image: 一只无色气球悬在空气中，旁边一株豆科植物的根瘤被剖开露出粉红色内部
scene: 农夫轮种豆科作物，让土壤里的氮多起来，不必再买化肥。 The farmer rotated legumes to add nitrogen to the soil without buying fertilizer.
sceneCN: 这里 nitrogen 指「土壤中的氮素养分」（第 3 个义项：氮肥与固氮）；豆科植物的根瘤菌把空气中的氮固定进土壤，农户因此不必买化肥。图中可辨识物件：豆科植株、根瘤剖面、土壤层、轮作示意牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 氮；氮气（不可数；化学式 N₂）

senses.title: The element
senses.definition: the chemical element with atomic number 7, a non-metal that forms strong triple bonds in its diatomic form
senses.definitionCN: 原子序数为 7 的元素，非金属，其双原子形式含牢固的三键
senses.example: Nitrogen has seven protons and typically seven neutrons.
senses.exampleCN: 氮有七个质子，通常也有七个中子。
senses.why: The name labels an element, not just the air gas, so it also applies to nitrogen atoms inside proteins and fertilisers.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字标的是元素而非仅仅是空气里的气体，因此蛋白质与肥料中的氮原子同样适用。

senses.title: The bulk gas of the air
senses.titleCN: 大气主体：约占空气五分之四的惰性气体
senses.definition: molecular N2, the inert gas that dilutes oxygen and fills most of the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 双原子分子 N₂，稀释氧、占据大气绝大部分的惰性气体
senses.example: Crisp packets are filled with nitrogen to stop the contents going stale.
senses.exampleCN: 薯片包装充入氮气，防止内容物变陈。
senses.why: Because the triple bond makes N2 unreactive, industry values it precisely for doing nothing.
senses.whyCN: 由于三键使 N₂ 极不活泼，工业看重的恰恰是它「什么都不做」。

senses.title: Soil fertility and fixation
senses.titleCN: 土壤氮素：固氮、施肥与轮作
senses.definition: the nitrogen available to plants in soil, supplied by fertiliser or by bacteria that fix atmospheric gas
senses.definitionCN: 土壤中可供植物利用的氮，来自肥料或固氮细菌
senses.example: Legumes add nitrogen to the soil through their root nodules.
senses.exampleCN: 豆科植物通过根瘤给土壤补充氮。
senses.why: Plants cannot use N2 directly, so agricultural usage names the usable forms, not the gas overhead.
senses.whyCN: 植物无法直接利用 N₂，因此农业用法指的是可利用的形态，而不是头顶上的气体。

senses.title: Inside proteins
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质中的氮：氨基酸的基本成分
senses.definition: the nitrogen bound in amino acids, and therefore in every protein and in DNA
senses.definitionCN: 结合在氨基酸中、从而存在于每种蛋白质与 DNA 中的氮
senses.example: Every amino acid carries at least one nitrogen atom.
senses.exampleCN: 每种氨基酸都至少带有一个氮原子。
senses.why: Life's chemistry is built on nitrogen-containing groups, so the element doubles as a marker of protein content.
senses.whyCN: 生命的化学建立在含氮基团之上，因此这个元素也成了蛋白质含量的标记。

senses.title: Liquid nitrogen
senses.titleCN: 液氮：极低温的冷却与保存介质
senses.definition: nitrogen cooled to about minus 196 degrees Celsius, used for freezing, storage and cooling
senses.definitionCN: 冷却到约零下 196 摄氏度的氮，用于冷冻、保存与降温
senses.example: Samples are stored in liquid nitrogen at the tissue bank.
senses.exampleCN: 组织库中的样本保存在液氮里。
senses.why: The boiling point of the gas is so low that its liquid becomes a standard laboratory coolant.
senses.whyCN: 这种气体的沸点极低，其液态因此成了实验室的标准冷却剂。

senses.title: Nitrogen oxides and smog
senses.titleCN: 氮氧化物：交通排放与光化学烟雾
senses.definition: the family of nitrogen-oxygen compounds, especially NO and NO2, formed in hot engines and driving photochemical smog
senses.definitionCN: 氮与氧的化合物一族，尤其是高温引擎生成的 NO 与 NO₂，会促成光化学烟雾
senses.example: Nitrogen oxides from traffic feed the smog over the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 交通排放的氮氧化物助长了谷地上空的光化学烟雾。
senses.why: Pollution control needed a short collective label, so the element name stands in for its troublesome compounds.
senses.whyCN: 污染控制需要一个简短的统称，于是元素名被用来指代它那些麻烦的化合物。

senses.title: The nitrogen cycle
senses.titleCN: 氮循环：在空气、土壤与生物之间流转
senses.definition: the circulation of nitrogen among the atmosphere, soil, water and living things through fixation, assimilation and denitrification
senses.definitionCN: 氮经固氮、同化与反硝化在大气、土壤、水体与生物之间循环
senses.example: The nitrogen cycle moves the element between air, soil and living things.
senses.exampleCN: 氮循环让这个元素在空气、土壤与生物之间流转。
senses.why: Because the element changes chemical form at every step, the cycle is named after the element rather than any one compound.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个元素在每一步都改变化学形态，循环便以元素而非某一种化合物命名。

senses.title: The nitre-former in the name
senses.definition: the sense recorded by the name itself: Chaptal named the gas because it was found in nitre, that is, saltpetre
senses.definitionCN: 名字本身记录的义项：夏普塔尔因这种气体存在于硝石（硝酸钾）中而为它命名
senses.example: The name nitrogen still says 'nitre-former', though the gas itself is inert.
senses.exampleCN: nitrogen 这个名字至今仍表示「硝石产生者」，尽管这种气体本身是惰性的。
senses.why: The French coinage nitrogene described where the element came from chemically, and English simply transliterated the claim.
senses.whyCN: 法语造词 nitrogene 描述的是该元素在化学上的来源，英语只是把这个说法音译过来。

intro.en: Nitrogen is a French scientific coinage of 1790, built from Greek nitron 'soda, nitre' and -genes 'producer'. Its first element was already ambiguous in ancient Greek.
intro.cn: nitrogen 是 1790 年的法语科学造词，由希腊 nitron「碱、硝石」与 -genes「产生者」构成。它的第一块在古代希腊语中就已含混。

items.en: Greek nitron named native soda, a mineral salt used in cleaning, not saltpetre. Latin nitrum later shifted the word toward saltpetre, and chemistry inherited the confusion.
items.cn: 希腊 nitron 指天然碱，一种用于洗涤的矿物盐，而非硝石。拉丁 nitrum 后来把这个词引向硝石，化学继承了这一混淆。

items.en: The suffix -genes 'born of, producing' comes from the root gen- 'to be born'. It marks the element as something that generates a named substance.
items.cn: 后缀 -genes「由……所生、产生」出自词根 gen-「出生」。它把这个元素标记为能生成某种特定物质的东西。

items.en: In 1790 the French chemist Chaptal coined nitrogene, because the gas was obtained from nitre and seemed to be the nitre-forming principle. The claim was later revised.
items.cn: 1790 年法国化学家夏普塔尔造出 nitrogene，因为这种气体可从硝石取得，似乎是成硝石的本原。这一说法后来被修正。

items.en: English nitrogen appears in the 1790s, transliterating the French term as the new chemistry spread. Before that the gas was called 'dephlogisticated air' or 'mephitic air'.
items.cn: 英语 nitrogen 在 1790 年代出现，随新化学的传播音译了法语术语。在此以前，这种气体被称作「脱燃素空气」或「毒气」。

items.en: Once the element rather than the compound became the unit of chemistry, nitrogen named element 7 and its compounds were renamed as nitrides, nitrates and oxides.
items.cn: 当化学的单位从化合物转为元素后，nitrogen 成为 7 号元素的名称，其化合物则改称氮化物、硝酸盐与氧化物。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and whether Chaptal or a colleague first suggested the form nitrogene is debated; Greek nitron itself has no agreed deeper origin.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见的确切书证年代存疑，nitrogene 这一形式由夏普塔尔还是其同僚最先提出仍有争议；希腊 nitron 本身的更深来源也无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words sharing the nitre root whose chemistry differs sharply; the second holds other atmospheric gases that are often confused with nitrogen.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「硝石」词根但化学性质差别很大的词；第二组是常与氮混淆的其他大气气体。

entries.definition: A salt or ester of nitric acid, containing the NO3 group, such as potassium nitrate in fertiliser. Nitrogen is the element; nitrate is one of its compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 硝酸的盐或酯，含 NO₃ 基团，如肥料中的硝酸钾。nitrogen 是元素，nitrate 是它的化合物之一。

entries.definition: A salt containing the NO2 group, used in cured meat and formed in soil as an intermediate step of nitrification.
entries.definitionCN: 含 NO₂ 基团的盐，用于腌肉，也在土壤中作为硝化过程的中间产物生成。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'containing nitrogen', as in nitrogenous waste. It describes a material, not the element itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「含氮的」的形容词，如含氮废物。它描述材料，而不是元素本身。

entries.definition: The gas that makes up about a fifth of the air and supports combustion and respiration. Nitrogen dilutes it and does not burn.
entries.definitionCN: 约占空气五分之一、支持燃烧与呼吸的气体。氮稀释它，且自身不燃烧。

entries.definition: A noble gas making up about one percent of the air, even less reactive than nitrogen. It is used where an absolutely inert atmosphere is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 约占空气百分之一的稀有气体，比氮更不活泼。需要绝对惰性气氛时就用它。

entries.definition: NH3, a pungent gas made industrially from nitrogen and hydrogen. It is the form in which nitrogen is turned into fertiliser.
entries.definitionCN: NH₃，工业上用氮与氢合成的刺激性气体。它正是氮被转化为肥料时所采取的形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek nitron 'nitre' + -genes 'producer': the nitre-former, a name kept from a chemical claim.
normal.cn: 希腊 nitron「硝石」+ -genes「产生者」：成硝石者，一个源自化学主张的名字。

normal.en: The family runs nitrogenous, nitrate, nitrite, nitrify, denitrify and nitrogenase.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nitrogenous、nitrate、nitrite、nitrify、denitrify、nitrogenase。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: nitrogen fixation, nitrogen cycle, liquid nitrogen, nitrogen oxides.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：固氮、氮循环、液氮、氮氧化物。

normal.en: Air is about four fifths nitrogen and one fifth oxygen.
normal.cn: 空气约五分之四是氮，五分之一是氧。

normal.en: Legumes fix nitrogen through root nodules, which is why farmers rotate them.
normal.cn: 豆科植物靠根瘤固氮，这也是农户进行轮作的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a bag of crisps puffed up with a gas that keeps every chip crisp.
abstract.cn: 想象一袋薯片鼓鼓的，里面充着一种让每片都保持酥脆的气体。

abstract.en: Picture a root nodule sliced open, pink inside, quietly turning air into soil fertility.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗根瘤被切开，内部粉红，正悄悄把空气变成土壤肥力。

abstract.en: Picture white vapour pouring off liquid nitrogen and rolling across the laboratory bench.
abstract.cn: 想象液氮上方涌出白色雾气，沿着实验台漫开。

examples.en: Nitrogen makes up roughly seventy-eight percent of the atmosphere.
examples.cn: 氮约占大气的百分之七十八。

examples.en: Excess nitrogen runoff from farms feeds algal blooms downstream.
examples.cn: 农场过量的氮径流在下游催生藻华。

examples.en: The welding shop uses nitrogen to purge oxygen from the pipes.
examples.cn: 焊接车间用氮把管道中的氧排净。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nitro（硝石）+ gen（产生）」——从硝石中得来的元素 → nitrogen 氮

root: 希腊 nitron「天然碱、硝石」+ -genes「产生者」→ 法语 nitrogene（1790，夏普塔尔）→ 英语 nitrogen。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one element from the periodic table through air, soil, protein, coolant, smog and the nitrogen cycle, ending with the naming claim that still sits inside the word.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个元素从周期表走进空气、土壤、蛋白质、冷却剂、烟雾与氮循环，最后落在仍留在词里的那个命名主张上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a colourless gas everywhere and a sliced pink root nodule.
core.cn: 核心意象：无处不在的无色气体，与一颗切开的粉色根瘤。

branches.en: THE ATOM: element 7 is defined by seven protons and its triple bond.
branches.cn: 原子：7 号元素由七个质子与三键定义。

branches.en: THE BULK GAS: inertness is a property, so packaging and welding value it for what it does not do.
branches.cn: 主体气体：惰性本身即特性，包装与焊接看重的正是它「不做什么」。

branches.en: THE CYCLE: soil fertility and global circulation describe the same element changing form.
branches.cn: 循环：土壤肥力与全球循环描述的是同一元素不断变换形态。

branches.en: LIFE: amino acids and DNA make nitrogen a marker of living matter.
branches.cn: 生命：氨基酸与 DNA 使氮成为生命物质的标记。

branches.en: USES AND CLAIMS: liquid coolant, polluting oxides and the nitre story all hang off the same name.
branches.cn: 用途与说法：液氮冷却、污染性氧化物与硝石故事，都挂在同一个名字上。

intro.en: Nitrogen is a scientific compound of a Greek noun for nitre and a Greek suffix for producing, reshaped in French and then borrowed into English.
intro.cn: nitrogen 是科学造词：希腊语表示硝石的名词加希腊语表示产生的后缀，经法语改写后借入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin nitrum carried the nitre sense, and New Latin nitrogenium fixed the element name so that nitrate, nitrite and nitride could be built from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nitrum 承载了「硝石」义，新拉丁语 nitrogenium 固定了元素名，使 nitrate、nitrite 与 nitride 得以由它构成。

items.meaningCN: 7 号元素及其双原子气体

items.example: Nitrogenous waste builds up in the tank.
items.exampleCN: 含氮废物在水箱中累积。

items.example: Nitrate levels in the well are too high.
items.exampleCN: 井水中的硝酸盐含量过高。

items.example: Nitrite is used to cure ham.
items.exampleCN: 亚硝酸盐用于腌制火腿。

items.meaning: to convert into nitrate by bacterial action
items.meaningCN: 经细菌作用转化为硝酸盐
items.example: Bacteria nitrify the ammonia in the soil.
items.exampleCN: 细菌把土壤中的氨硝化。

items.meaning: to convert nitrate back into nitrogen gas
items.exampleCN: 潮湿土壤会迅速反硝化。

items.meaning: the enzyme that fixes atmospheric nitrogen
items.exampleCN: 固氮酶只能在无氧条件下工作。

items.meaning: a compound of nitrogen with a metal
items.meaningCN: 氮与金属形成的化合物

items.meaning: relating to the higher oxide of nitrogen
items.meaningCN: 与高价态氮氧化物有关的

definition_en: in a way that gives more than is expected
core_image: 主人不断往客人的碗里添菜
scene: 他慷慨地把奖金分给了同事。 He generously shared his bonus with his colleagues.
sceneCN: 这里 generously 是「慷慨地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他慷慨地把奖金分给了同事。

senses.title: In a giving way
senses.definition: in a way that gives money, help, or time freely
senses.definitionCN: 以乐于给予金钱、帮助或时间的方式
senses.example: He generously shared his bonus with his colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 他慷慨地把奖金分给了同事。
senses.why: The adverb describes how an open-handed action is done.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词描述一个慷慨动作是以何种方式完成的。

senses.title: In large amounts
senses.definition: in amounts that are larger than usual
senses.definitionCN: 以比通常更大的量
senses.example: The table was generously spread with food.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上丰盛地摆满了食物。
senses.why: Giving generously often shows up as plenty on the table.
senses.whyCN: 慷慨地给予，常常表现为桌上的丰盛。

senses.title: With kindness
senses.definition: in a kind and fair way, especially in judging others
senses.definitionCN: 以友善公正的方式，尤其在评价他人时
senses.example: She spoke generously of her rival.
senses.exampleCN: 她宽厚地称赞了她的对手。
senses.why: The giving spirit extends from things to words.
senses.whyCN: 给予的精神从事物延伸到了言语。

intro.en: Generously is the adverb built from generous and -ly.
intro.cn: generously 是由 generous 加 -ly 构成的副词。

items.en: Generosus meant of noble birth.
items.cn: generosus 意为出身高贵的。

items.en: French kept the word as generous.
items.cn: 法语保留了 generous 这个词形。

items.en: English used generous for noble character.
items.cn: 英语用 generous 表示品格高贵。

items.en: The adverb generously added the -ly ending.
items.cn: 副词 generously 加上了 -ly 后缀。

items.en: It came to describe both giving and plentiful amounts.
items.cn: 它逐渐同时描述给予行为和丰盛的数量。

note.en: Generously is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of kind giving.

normalIntro.en: To do something generously is to do it with an open hand.
normalIntro.cn: 慷慨地做某事，就是张开手去做。

normal.en: He generously shared his bonus with his colleagues.
normal.cn: 他慷慨地把奖金分给了同事。

normal.en: The table was generously spread with food.
normal.cn: 桌上丰盛地摆满了食物。

normal.en: She spoke generously of her rival.
normal.cn: 她宽厚地称赞了她的对手。

normal.en: The library was generously supported by local firms.

normal.en: Please give generously to the food bank.
normal.cn: 请向食物银行慷慨解囊。

abstract.en: Give generously and count nothing twice.
abstract.cn: 慷慨地给，别把给出去的东西再数一遍。

abstract.en: A full table is a sentence in the language of care.
abstract.cn: 一桌丰盛的食物，是用关怀写成的句子。

abstract.en: Praise given freely costs little and travels far.
abstract.cn: 自由给出的赞美代价很小，却能传得很远。

dict_mnemonic.text: generously 就是 generous（慷慨的）加 -ly 变成副词：give generously 是「慷慨解囊」，generously spread 是「丰盛地摆满」，speak generously of 是「宽厚地称赞」。

root: 由 generous（慷慨的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 generosus（出身高贵的）。

sensesIntro.en: Generously means in a giving way, in large amounts, or with kindness.
sensesIntro.cn: generously 意为以给予的方式、以大量的方式，或以宽厚的方式。

core.en: Acting with an open hand and a generous measure.
core.cn: 以张开的手和宽大的分量去行动。

branches.en: The host keeps filling every bowl.
branches.cn: 主人不停地给每个碗添满。

branches.en: Food covers the table from edge to edge.
branches.cn: 食物从桌子这头铺到那头。

branches.en: A rival is praised without a sting.
branches.cn: 对手被称赞时话里不带刺。

branches.en: Giving often and giving much look the same.
branches.cn: 经常给和给得多，看起来是一回事。

branches.en: Plenty at the table and warmth in words go together.
branches.cn: 桌上的丰盛与言语里的温暖总是相伴。

intro.en: Generously adds the adverb ending to the generous family.
intro.cn: generously 给 generous 词族加上副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root generosus meant noble by birth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 generosus 意为出身高贵的。

items.example: They generously offered us a room.

一位慷慨的主人迎接了我们。

items.example: The critics praised the film overgenerously.
items.exampleCN: 影评人过于慷慨地称赞了这部电影。
他的慷慨大方广为人知。
一位心地慷慨的老师留到很晚。

latinEntries.exampleCN: generosus 是 generously 的源头。

definition_en: an accident in which two moving objects hit each other, or a serious disagreement between ideas or people
core_image: 两辆车在路口来不及刹车的那一瞬
scene: 雨夜的路口，一辆货车突然转向。 Two cars were badly damaged in the collision.
sceneCN: 这里 collision 指「碰撞」（第 1 个义项：两物相撞）；句意是两辆车在碰撞中严重受损。

senses.title: Two objects hitting
senses.definition: an accident in which two moving objects hit each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个运动物体互相撞上的事故
senses.example: The collision broke the front of the truck.
senses.exampleCN: 碰撞撞坏了卡车的前部。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to strike together, and the noun names that single moment.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为撞到一起，名词命名的就是那一瞬。

senses.title: A clash of ideas or interests
senses.definition: a serious disagreement between people, ideas or interests
senses.definitionCN: 人、观念或利益之间的严重冲突
senses.example: A collision of opinions delayed the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 意见冲突使表决推迟。
senses.why: Two arguments can strike like two vehicles when neither will turn.
senses.whyCN: 两种主张各不相让，就会像两辆车一样撞上。

intro.en: Collision comes from Latin collisio, from com- together and laedere, to strike.
intro.cn: collision 出自拉丁语 collisio，由 com-（一起）与 laedere（撞击）组成。

items.en: Laedere meant to strike or injure.
items.cn: laedere 意为撞击或伤害。

items.en: Collidere meant to strike two things together.
items.cn: collidere 意为把两物撞在一起。

items.en: Collisio named the striking itself.
items.cn: collisio 指撞击这件事。

items.en: French collision brought the noun into English.
items.cn: 法语 collision 把这个名词带进英语。

items.en: The word now also covers clashes of ideas.
items.cn: 这个词如今也涵盖观念冲突。

note.en: The look-alike group holds nouns ending in the same sound, while the meaning group names hits and disagreements.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾同音的名词，近义组列出撞击与分歧。

entries.definition: secret cooperation for a dishonest purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为不正当目的暗中串通

entries.definition: a choice that has been made
the act of splitting something into parts
a violent hit involving vehicles
the force of one object hitting another
entries.definitionCN: 一物撞击另一物的力量

entries.definition: a serious disagreement or struggle

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold the picture of two moving bodies meeting, then transfer it to ideas.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子抓住两个运动物相撞的画面，再把它挪到观念上。

normal.en: Collision hides collide, the verb that names the act.
normal.cn: collision 里藏着动词 collide，动作就由它命名。

normal.en: The prefix com- means together, so two things arrive at one point.
normal.cn: 前缀 com- 意为一起，所以两样东西到了同一点。

normal.en: The ending -sion often marks a noun of action, like decision.
normal.cn: 词尾 -sion 常标示动作名词，例如 decision。

normal.en: Cars, ships and aircraft can all be in collision.
normal.cn: 汽车、船只和飞机都可能发生碰撞。

normal.en: When two opinions refuse to turn, that is also a collision.
normal.cn: 两种意见都不肯转向时，那也是一种冲突。

abstract.en: Picture two bright headlights closing on one narrow bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象两束车灯在同一座窄桥上逼近。

abstract.en: Picture a scatter of glass on wet asphalt.
abstract.cn: 想象湿沥青上散落着碎玻璃。

abstract.en: Picture two people rising at a meeting, both refusing to yield.
abstract.cn: 想象会上两人同时起身，谁都不肯让步。

examples.en: The collision happened at a quiet crossroads.
examples.cn: 碰撞发生在一个安静的路口。

examples.en: Helmets reduce the damage of a collision.
examples.cn: 头盔能减轻碰撞造成的伤害。

examples.en: A collision between duty and desire kept him awake.
examples.cn: 责任与欲望的冲突让他睡不着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collision 记成 collide 加 sion：两物撞到同一点，就是碰撞。

root: 源自拉丁语 collisio，由 collidere（撞到一起）派生，com- 表一起，laedere 表撞击。

sensesIntro.en: From metal meeting metal on a road to two firm opinions meeting in a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 从路上金属撞金属，到屋里两种坚决的意见相撞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths crossing at the same point at the same second.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路线在同一秒交于同一点。

branches.en: The physical sense is the oldest and most concrete.
branches.cn: 物理碰撞义最古老也最具体。

branches.en: The abstract sense keeps the same picture of two forces meeting.
branches.cn: 抽象义保留的仍是两种力量相遇的画面。

branches.en: Both senses need two parties and no room to turn.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要两方且无处可让。

branches.en: Insurance reports use the word for any vehicle hit.
branches.cn: 保险报告用这个词指任何车辆撞击。

branches.en: A collision of interests can stop a whole project.
branches.cn: 利益冲突能让整个项目停摆。

intro.en: The family is built on collide, with -sion for the event and -er for the machine.
intro.cn: 这个词族建在 collide 上，-sion 表事件，-er 表机器。

latinIntro.en: Collidere and laedere are the Latin sources of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: collidere 与 laedere 是整组词的拉丁语来源。

items.meaning: more than one crash or clash
items.example: Most collisions happen close to home.
items.exampleCN: 多数碰撞发生在离家不远的地方。

items.example: The two ships collided in fog.
The van collided with a bus.
items.exampleCN: 货车撞上了一辆公交车。

items.meaning: hitting each other at this moment
items.example: Two streams of air were colliding.

items.meaning: a machine that makes particles collide
items.example: The collider runs in a long tunnel.
items.exampleCN: 这台对撞机在一条长隧道中运行。

items.meaning: a crash in which fronts meet
items.example: A head-on collision closed the road.
items.exampleCN: 一场正面相撞封闭了道路。

items.meaning: a crash between two aircraft in flight
items.meaningCN: 两架飞行器在空中相撞
items.example: The report studied the mid-air collision.
items.exampleCN: 报告研究了这起空中相撞。

latinEntries.example: Collidere is the verb behind collision.
latinEntries.exampleCN: collidere 是 collision 背后的动词。

latinEntries.example: Laedere supplies the second half of collidere.
latinEntries.exampleCN: laedere 提供了 collidere 的后半部分。

definition_zh: 使残疾；严重削弱；使瘫痪
definition_en: to make a person unable to walk, or to damage something severely
core_image: 一个人扶着墙艰难移动，一条腿再也使不上力
scene: 一场事故之后，他扶着墙走，右腿再也使不上力。 The injury could cripple him for life.
sceneCN: 这里 cripple 指「使残疾」（第 1 个义项：使某人丧失行走或行动能力）；句意是这处伤可能让他终身残疾。

pos.zh: 使残疾；严重削弱；使瘫痪
行动不便的人（含冒犯，宜避免使用）

senses.title: Make unable to walk
senses.definition: to damage a person's body so that walking becomes hard or impossible
senses.definitionCN: 损伤人的身体，使行走变得困难或不可能
senses.example: The accident crippled his left leg.
senses.exampleCN: 那场事故使他的左腿残疾。
senses.why: A joint that cannot bear weight removes a whole way of moving.
senses.whyCN: 一个不能承重的关节，就带走了一整种移动方式。

senses.title: Damage a system severely
senses.definition: to damage a system, group or machine so that it works badly
senses.definitionCN: 严重损伤一个系统、团体或机器，使其难以运转
senses.example: The storm crippled the railway for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴使铁路瘫痪了一周。
senses.why: A body and a system both fail when one key part gives way.
senses.whyCN: 身体和系统一样，只要一个关键部件垮掉就失灵。

senses.title: Bring to a halt
senses.definition: to stop something from moving or acting at all
senses.definitionCN: 使某物完全不能移动或行动
senses.example: Fear can cripple a whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 恐惧能让整支队伍动弹不得。
senses.why: The strongest force is often the one that simply stops motion.
senses.whyCN: 最强的力量，往往只是把运动停住。

intro.en: Cripple comes from Old English crypel, one who can only creep, from the same root as creep.
intro.cn: cripple 源自古英语 crypel（只能爬行的人），与 creep 同根。

items.en: Crypel named a person who could only creep.
items.cn: crypel 指只能爬行的人。

items.en: It came from the same root as creep.
items.cn: 它与 creep 出自同一个词根。

items.en: Cripel described a body that could not stand straight.
items.cn: cripel 形容无法站直的身体。

items.en: The verb meant to make a person lame.
items.cn: 动词形式意为使人变瘸。

items.en: It was used for ships and for economies.
items.cn: 它被用来形容船只和经济。

items.en: The noun is now often seen as offensive.
items.cn: 今天这个名词常被视为冒犯。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cripp- spelling, and the meaning group names other ways of damaging or blocking.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cripp- 这串拼写，近义组列出其他损伤与阻断的说法。

entries.definition: badly damaged or unable to move
entries.definitionCN: 严重受损或无法行动的

entries.definition: so heavy that it stops all action
to move low and slowly
to make a person unable to act normally
to make something less strong
to make a body or system unable to move
entries.definitionCN: 使身体或系统无法运转

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a leg that cannot bear weight and end with a stalled railway.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一条不能承重的腿开始，最后落到停摆的铁路。

normal.en: Cripple is a cousin of creep: a body forced down low.
normal.cn: cripple 是 creep 的表亲：一具被迫压低的身体。

normal.en: One bad joint can stop a whole walk.
normal.cn: 一个坏关节，就能让整段路走不成。

normal.en: A storm cripples trains the way a stone cripples a wheel.
normal.cn: 风暴让火车瘫痪，就像石子让车轮失灵。

normal.en: Debt is a heavy boot on a small company.
normal.cn: 债务是一只踩在小公司身上的重靴。

normal.en: Use the noun with care; it can wound as much as an injury.
normal.cn: 用这个名词要小心，它伤人可能不亚于伤病。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed against a wall for support.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着墙借力。

abstract.en: Picture a rail line bent out of shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被扭得变形的铁轨。

abstract.en: Picture a team frozen in fear.
abstract.cn: 想象一支被恐惧定住的队伍。

examples.en: The disease left him crippled for life.
examples.cn: 这场病让他落下了终身残疾。

examples.en: High debts crippled the small firm.
examples.cn: 高额债务拖垮了这家小公司。

examples.en: The snowstorm crippled the airport for two days.
examples.cn: 这场暴雪让机场瘫痪了两天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cripple 记成 creep（爬）的亲戚：站不起来、只能爬的人，就是被伤到无法行走。

root: 源自古英语 crypel（只能爬行的人），与 creep 同根；本义指无法直立行走的人，后作动词表示使人残疾，再引申为严重削弱或使系统瘫痪。

sensesIntro.en: From a body that cannot walk, to a system that cannot run, to a team that cannot move.
sensesIntro.cn: 从走不动的身体，到运转不了的系统，再到动不了的队伍。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a wall and a leg that will not hold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶墙，一条腿再也撑不住。

branches.en: An injury takes away the power to walk.
branches.cn: 一处伤带走了行走的能力。

branches.en: A storm or a debt can do the same to a system.
branches.cn: 风暴或债务也能对系统做出同样的事。

branches.en: Fear alone can bring all movement to zero.
branches.cn: 光是恐惧，就能把一切行动归零。

branches.en: Body and machine both fail at one weak point.
branches.cn: 身体和机器都栽在一个薄弱处。

branches.en: Damage first slows work, then stops it.
branches.cn: 损伤先让活儿变慢，再让它停住。

intro.en: Cripple is a native English word, and its family grows with -ed, -ing and -ware.
intro.cn: cripple 是英语本族词，它的家族靠 -ed、-ing 与 -ware 生长。

latinIntro.en: No Latin base is involved; the root is the old Germanic word for creeping.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词基，它的根是日耳曼语里表示爬行的老词。

items.example: The fall crippled his right arm.
items.exampleCN: 这一跤使他的右臂残了。

items.example: The crippled ship limped into port.
items.exampleCN: 受损的船勉强驶进港口。

items.meaning: so heavy that it stops action
items.exampleCN: 这家人面对压垮人的开销。

items.example: The town was cripplingly short of water.
items.exampleCN: 镇上缺水缺到难以维持。

items.example: The storm was a crippler for farmers.
items.exampleCN: 这场风暴对农户是致命一击。

items.meaningCN: 被人为限制功能的软件
items.exampleCN: 免费版是功能受限的软件。

items.example: A cat can creep without a sound.

items.exampleCN: 蔓延的杂草占满了小路。

definition_zh: 分配；拨给；分派（任务）；把（成本）分摊到科目
definition_en: to give out money, time, or resources for a particular purpose, or to assign a duty or cost to someone
core_image: 一张长桌上摆着几只空盘子，厨师按人数把菜一份份分进去
scene: 市政会议开到深夜，争论的焦点是钱该往哪里花。 The council allocated half the budget to road repairs.
sceneCN: 这里的 allocate 是「分配、拨给」（第 1 个义项：把钱或资源按用途分出）；句意是市议会把一半预算拨给了道路维修。

pos.zh: 动词：分配；拨给；分派；分摊

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -tion 构成，义为「分配；拨款；配额」
由 re- 加 allocate 构成，义为「重新分配」
由 allocation 加 -ive 构成，义为「与分配有关的」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「分配者；分配程序」

senses.title: To give out money or resources
senses.definition: to set apart and give out money, materials, or other resources for a stated purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途划出并发放资金、物资或其他资源
senses.example: The hospital allocated two million pounds to new equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 医院拨出两百万英镑购置新设备。
senses.why: Latin locare meant 'to place', and ad- added 'to'; to allocate is to place something into a particular slot, so money is put where the purpose requires it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locare 意为「放置」，ad- 表示「到」；allocate 就是「放到某个位置上」，钱被放进为它指定的那一格，所以既可译「分配」也可译「拨给」。

senses.title: To assign a duty or role
senses.definition: to give a particular job, duty, or role to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把某项工作、职责或角色交给某个人或某个群体
senses.example: The teacher allocated each group a different part of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把项目的不同部分分派给各个小组。
senses.why: The same 'placing' works for tasks: a duty is put into someone's hands, and the person becomes the slot it occupies.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「放置」也适用于任务：职责被放进某人手里，那个人就成了这项职责所在的位置，因此 allocate 常与 tasks、duties、roles 搭配。

senses.title: To apportion costs in accounting
senses.definition: to divide a cost or revenue among accounts, departments, or periods in bookkeeping
senses.definitionCN: 在记账中把成本或收入分摊到各科目、各部门或各期间
senses.example: The firm allocated the overhead costs across its three branches.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把间接费用分摊到三个分部。
senses.why: In accounting the 'placing' becomes a division: one total is cut into shares and each share is placed on the account that caused it, which is why the verb appears with costs and overhead.
senses.whyCN: 在会计里，「放置」变成了「切分」：一笔总额被切成若干份，每一份放进造成它的那个科目，所以这个义项的宾语常见 costs、overhead 这类词。

intro.en: Allocate is a bookkeeping word at heart: it comes from a Latin verb for placing something in a spot.
intro.cn: allocate 骨子里是个记账词：它来自拉丁语中表示「把东西放到某处」的动词。

items.en: locus meant 'place, spot', and it also gave English local and locate.
items.cn: locus 意为「地方、位置」，英语的 local 与 locate 也由它而来。

items.en: locare meant 'to place, set, arrange', and was used of putting things or persons in position.
items.cn: locare 意为「放置、安置、安排」，用于把物品或人放到位置上。

items.en: The prefixed form allocare is recorded in medieval Latin with the sense 'to place to, assign', especially in accounts.
items.cn: 加前缀的形式 allocare 见于中世纪拉丁语，义为「放置到、分派」，尤用于账目。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; early examples already concern money and shares.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，早期用例已经与钱款和份额有关。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb from budgets to tasks, seats, time slots, and computing memory.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从预算扩展到任务、座位、时间段以及计算机内存。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb for placing; the near-meaning group gathers ways of giving out shares with different emphasis.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「放置」动词；近义组收发放份额的各种说法，侧重各有不同。

to find the place of something, or to place it

normalIntro.en: Allocate puts things into places: money into a budget line, tasks into hands, costs onto accounts.
normalIntro.cn: allocate 是把东西放进位置：钱进预算项，任务进手里，成本进科目。

normal.en: Remember locus, 'place': allocate means to place out.
normal.cn: 记住 locus「位置」：allocate 就是把东西分放到各处。

normal.en: The common pattern is allocate something to someone.
normal.cn: 常见句型是 allocate something to someone。

normal.en: The noun is allocation, with -tion.
normal.cn: 名词是 allocation，加 -tion。

normal.en: Do not spell it with a double l in the middle.
normal.cn: 中间不要写成双写 l。

normal.en: Costs can be allocated as well as money.
normal.cn: 除了钱，成本也可以用这个词分摊。

examples.en: The government allocated more money to rural schools this year.

examples.en: Each team leader allocated the work according to people's strengths.

examples.en: The accountant allocated part of the rent to the storage room.

definition_zh: 手工的；手动的；体力的；手册；手动挡汽车；手键盘
definition_en: done or operated by the hands rather than by machine or automatically; as a noun, a book of instructions, a hand-played keyboard, or a car with a manual gearbox
core_image: 一只沾着机油的手掌托着一本薄册：既能亲手操作，也能一手拿起
scene: 修车铺里，技师翻开油污的手册。 He opened the oily manual to page forty-two and tightened the bolts with a hand wrench, following the drawing exactly.
sceneCN: 这里 manual 是「手册」（第 4 个义项：一手可持的手册）；句意：他翻开油污的手册到第 42 页，照图示用手动扳手拧紧螺栓。图中可辨识物件：维修手册、扳手、发动机舱、螺栓；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 手册；说明书；手动挡；手键盘

derivatives.zh: 手语教学法；主张手工训练的教育观点
主张手工训练者；手语教学者
手册化的；按手册标准化操作的

senses.title: Done with the hands, not by machine
senses.titleCN: 用手完成，而非机器完成
senses.definition: done, made, or performed with the hands rather than by machine or tool
senses.definitionCN: 用手而不是机器或工具完成、制作或执行
senses.example: The wall was built by manual labour, stone by stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙是靠手工劳动一块石头一块石头砌成的。
senses.why: Latin manualis meant 'of or belonging to the hand', from manus 'hand'. The adjective's first job in English, around 1400, was to mark work done by hand, so the hand is the defining instrument.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 manualis 意为“属于手的”，来自 manus“手”。这个形容词约在 1400 年进入英语时的第一项任务，就是标记“用手完成的工作”，因此手是定义性的工具。

senses.title: Hand-operated: a control that bypasses the machine
senses.titleCN: 手动操作：绕开自动装置的控制
senses.definition: of a device or control, operated by physical hand movement rather than automatically
senses.definitionCN: 指装置或控制件靠手的实际动作操作，而不是自动运行
senses.example: If the sensor fails, use the manual override beside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 如果传感器失灵，就用门旁的手动超控装置。
senses.why: Here the contrast is not hand versus machine in general but hand versus automatic. A manual switch exists so that a person can take over from the system, which is why manual also means 'not automatic'.
senses.whyCN: 这里对比的不是泛泛的“手与机器”，而是“手动与自动”。手动开关的存在，就是为了让人能从系统手里接管，因此 manual 也引申为“非自动的”。

senses.title: Physical rather than mental work
senses.titleCN: 体力工作，而非脑力工作
senses.definition: of work or a worker, involving bodily effort rather than office or intellectual work
senses.definitionCN: 指工作或劳动者需要体力，而不是办公室或脑力工作
senses.example: The factory replaced most manual jobs with automated lines.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂用自动化生产线取代了大多数体力岗位。
senses.why: The hand is the body's most obvious working part, so manual work became a social category opposed to head work. The word now describes a class of employment, not just a method.
senses.whyCN: 手是身体最明显的工作部位，因此 manual work 成了与“脑力工作”相对的社会类别。这个词现在描述的是一类就业，而不只是一种方法。

senses.title: The handbook you hold in one hand
senses.definition: a book giving instructions, rules, or reference information for a device, course, or job
senses.definitionCN: 为装置、课程或工作提供说明、规则或参考信息的书
senses.example: Read the manual before you change the filter.
senses.exampleCN: 换滤芯之前先读说明书。
senses.why: The noun is recorded in the early 15c. for a small service book, and by the 1530s for any concise handbook. The etymological picture is a small book that can be carried or used in one hand — the same hand returns.
senses.whyCN: 名词义在 15 世纪早期记录为小型的礼仪书，16 世纪 30 年代起指任何简明手册。词源画面是一本可以随身携带、或一手使用的小书——同一只手又回来了。

senses.title: A car you shift yourself
senses.definition: in informal use, a car with a manual gearbox, as opposed to an automatic
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指带手动变速器的汽车，与自动挡相对
senses.example: I learned to drive on a manual and still prefer one.
senses.exampleCN: 我是开手动挡学会开车的，现在仍然更喜欢手动挡。
senses.why: The adjective manual transmission is shortened to the noun 'a manual'. The hand is now on the gear lever, so the word names the car by the kind of control it demands.
senses.whyCN: 形容词短语 manual transmission 被缩略成名词 a manual。此时手放在换挡杆上，于是这个词用“它要求哪种控制方式”来给车命名。

senses.title: The keyboard played by hand
senses.definition: one of the hand-played keyboards of an organ, as opposed to the pedal keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 管风琴上用手演奏的键盘之一，与脚踏键盘相对
senses.example: The organist moves between the swell manual and the great manual.
senses.exampleCN: 管风琴手在强弱手键盘与主手键盘之间切换。
senses.why: In organ music, manuals are the rows played by hand and the pedals are played by foot. The adjective becomes a noun because the hand is what distinguishes this keyboard from the other.
senses.whyCN: 在管风琴音乐中，manual 是用手弹的键盘排，pedal 是用脚踩的。形容词转为名词，因为“用手”正是这组键盘区别于另一组的地方。

senses.title: The prescribed drill: manual exercise
senses.titleCN: 规定的操练：军事手册操典
senses.definition: in military history, the prescribed routine for handling a rifle or weapon, known as manual exercise
senses.definitionCN: 军事史上规定的步枪或武器操作程序，称为 manual exercise
senses.example: Recruits spent a week learning the manual exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵花了一周学习武器操作操典。
senses.why: Manual exercise is recorded in 1760 as 'the art of handling the rifle and other arms with precision and according to the prescribed method'. Here manual means a fixed sequence performed by hand, not a book.
senses.whyCN: manual exercise 记录于 1760 年，意为“按既定方法精确操作步枪及其他武器的技艺”。这里的 manual 指的是一套用手完成的固定程序，而不是一本书。

senses.title: Usage boundary: manual, hand-made, menial
senses.definition: manual describes hand operation or a handbook; it does not automatically mean unskilled or low-status, and manual is not a synonym of menial
senses.definitionCN: manual 描述用手操作或手册；它不自动表示“无需技能”或“地位低”，也不是 menial 的同义词
senses.example: Manual work can be highly skilled: a watchmaker's hands are manual and expert.
senses.exampleCN: 体力/手工工作也可以高度专业化：制表师的手既是 manual 的，也是专业的。
senses.why: Manual names the instrument (the hand), while menial names the status (low, servile). A manual job may be skilled, and a menial job may involve little handwork at all. The boundary keeps the word technical rather than social.
senses.whyCN: manual 命名的是工具（手），menial 命名的是地位（低微、仆役性）。manual 的工作可能很专业，menial 的工作可能根本不需要多少手工。这条边界让这个词保持技术性，而不是社会评判。

intro.en: Manual is the Latin adjective for 'of the hand'. English first used it for hand-made work, then for hand-operated controls, and turned it into a noun for a small book that fits in one hand — the same hand at both ends.
intro.cn: manual 是拉丁语中表示“属于手的”形容词。英语先用它表示手工完成的工作，再表示手动控制，随后转为名词，指一本能拿在一只手里的小书——两端都是同一只手。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'of or pertaining to the hand; done, made, or used by hand', from Latin manualis.
items.cn: 约 1400 年首次记录为形容词，意为“属于手的；用手完成、制作或使用的”，来自拉丁语 manualis。

items.en: Latin manualis 'of or belonging to the hand; that can be thrown by hand', from manus 'hand, strength, power over; armed force; handwriting'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 manualis“属于手的；可以用手投掷的”，来自 manus“手、力量、支配权、武装力量、笔迹”。

items.en: manus is traced to PIE *man- (2) 'hand', the root also listed for manual, manage and manipulate. The reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: manus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *man-（第二支）“手”，也是 manual、manage、manipulate 所列的词根。该重构属于一般认为。

items.en: The noun appears meaning 'small service book used by a priest', from Old French manuel 'handbook' and Late Latin manuale 'case or cover of a book, handbook'.
items.cn: 名词义出现，指“神父使用的小型礼仪书”，来自古法语 manuel“手册”与晚期拉丁语 manuale“书套或书封、手册”。

items.en: The meaning 'a concise handbook of any sort' is recorded from the 1530s. Manual exercise, the prescribed handling of a rifle, appears in 1760.
items.cn: “任何类型的简明手册”义记录于 16 世纪 30 年代。manual exercise（规定的步枪操作）出现于 1760 年。

items.en: Modern English uses manual for hand operation, physical work, a handbook, a manual gearbox and an organ keyboard. The common thread is the hand, not a single object.
items.cn: 现代英语用 manual 表示手动操作、体力工作、手册、手动挡和管风琴手键盘。共同线索是“手”，而不是某一个固定物件。

note.en: The first group shares manus 'hand' or the manual shape. The second group separates the book sense from the hand-operated sense, which English keeps inside one word.
note.cn: 第一组共享 manus“手”或 manual 的词形。第二组把“书”的义项与“用手操作”的义项分开，而英语把它们放在同一个词里。

entries.definition: a metal ring for the wrist; to chain someone. It comes from Latin manicula, a diminutive of manus 'hand'.
entries.definitionCN: 手铐；给某人上镣铐。它来自拉丁语 manicula，是 manus“手”的指小形式。

entries.definition: a text written by hand rather than printed. It joins manus 'hand' with scriptum 'written'.
entries.definitionCN: 手写而非印刷的文本。它由 manus“手”+ scriptum“写”构成。

entries.definition: by hand, by means of the hand. It is the adverb from manual, recorded in the late 15c.
entries.definitionCN: 用手地；靠手完成地。它是 manual 的副词，记录于 15 世纪晚期。

entries.definition: a concise reference book. It is the closest synonym of manual in the book sense, and itself translates Latin manualis.
entries.definitionCN: 简明参考书。它是 manual 在“书”这一义项上最接近的同义词，本身正是对拉丁语 manualis 的翻译。

entries.definition: a book or person that shows the way. It is broader than manual: a guide may describe a city, while a manual explains how to operate something.
entries.definitionCN: 指路的书或人。它比 manual 更宽：guide 可以介绍一座城市，而 manual 说明如何操作某物。

entries.definition: worked by hand rather than automatically. It overlaps manual in the device sense but cannot mean a handbook.
entries.definitionCN: 用手而非自动操作的。它在装置义上与 manual 重叠，但不能表示手册。

entries.definition: relating to the body rather than the mind. Manual work is always physical, but physical work need not use the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体而非心智有关。manual 工作一定是体力/身体的，但体力工作不一定用手。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: manus 'hand' is the whole story, and it also appears in manuscript, manufacture, manicure, manacle and manage.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：manus“手”就是全部故事，它也出现在 manuscript、manufacture、manicure、manacle、manage 里。

normal.en: manualis is 'of the hand'. Manual labour is work of the hand; a manual is a book small enough for the hand; a manual gearbox is shifted by hand.
normal.cn: manualis 就是“属于手的”。manual labour 是手的劳动；manual 是一本一手可拿的书；manual gearbox 是用手换挡的变速箱。

normal.en: Hand and book meet in the noun: the etymological sense of manual is 'a small book such as may be carried in the hand'.
normal.cn: 手与书在名词义里相遇：manual 的词源义就是“一本可以拿在手里携带的小书”。

normal.en: Manual exercise (1760) is a fixed sequence of hand movements with a rifle, so manual can name a drill as well as a book.
normal.cn: manual exercise（1760）是一套用步枪完成的固定手部动作，所以 manual 也能指操典，而不只是书。

normal.en: Manual override exists so a person can take control back from an automatic system: manual means 'the human hand is still allowed in'.
normal.cn: manual override 的存在，是为了让人能从自动系统手里夺回控制权：manual 意味着“人的手仍然被允许介入”。

normal.en: Manuscript, manufacture and manicure all use manus: writing by hand, making by hand, caring for the hand.
normal.cn: manuscript、manufacture、manicure 都用 manus：手写、手做、照料手。

abstract.en: Picture a hand and a thin book: the hand can work without the book, and the book can be held by the hand. Manual lives where the two meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手和一本薄书：手可以不用书就工作，书可以被手拿着。manual 就活在这两者相遇的地方。

abstract.en: The same word covers the tool (hand), the mode (manual operation), the guide (handbook) and the object (a manual car). The hand is the hinge.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖工具（手）、方式（手动操作）、指南（手册）和物件（手动挡车）。手就是那个铰链。

abstract.en: When a machine automates the hand, manual becomes the exception that lets the hand return — a switch, a lever, an override.
abstract.cn: 当机器替代了手，manual 就成了让手回来的例外——一个开关、一根拉杆、一次超控。

examples.en: The manual explains how to reset the device in four steps.
examples.cn: 这本手册用四个步骤说明如何重置设备。

examples.en: Manual work is cheaper here, but slower than the new machine.
examples.cn: 这里的手工劳动更便宜，但比新机器慢。

examples.en: He prefers a manual because he likes choosing the gear.
examples.cn: 他更喜欢手动挡，因为他喜欢自己选挡位。

dict_mnemonic.text: “曼牛”——慢悠悠的牛拉着手工犁，旁边放着一本操作手册 → manual 手工的、手册

root: 拉丁语 manualis“属于手的”，来自 manus“手”，核心是“用手完成、用手操作”，并引申为“一手可持的小书”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of manual, all centred on the hand: work done by hand, a hand control, physical labour, a handbook held in one hand, a manual car, an organ keyboard, a rifle drill, and the boundary against menial.
sensesIntro.cn: manual 的八个义项都围绕手：用手完成的工作、手动控制、体力劳动、一手可持的手册、手动挡汽车、管风琴手键盘、步枪操典，以及它与 menial 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand does the work, and a thin book fits into that same hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：手完成工作，而一本薄书正好放进同一只手里。

branches.en: METHOD: work is done by hand rather than by machine.
branches.cn: 方式：工作靠手完成，而不是靠机器。

branches.en: CONTROL: a switch, a gear lever, an organ keyboard and a rifle drill all place the hand on a control.
branches.cn: 控制：开关、换挡杆、管风琴键盘与步枪操典，都把放在控制件上的手作为核心。

branches.en: LABOUR: handwork becomes a social category opposed to mental or office work.
branches.cn: 劳动：手工成为与脑力或办公室工作相对的社会类别。

branches.en: BOOK: a handbook is defined by being small enough to hold and use in one hand.
branches.cn: 书：手册之所以是手册，在于它小到可以一手拿着使用。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: manual names the instrument, not the status, so it never becomes menial by itself.
branches.cn: 边界：manual 命名工具，不命名地位，因此它本身从不等于 menial。

intro.en: Manual has no live English prefix. Its Latin stem manualis is frozen inside; English adds -ly, -ism and -ist, and forms compounds such as manual transmission and manual override.
intro.cn: manual 没有活的英语前缀。它的拉丁词干 manualis 凝固在词内；英语加 -ly、-ism、-ist，并构成 manual transmission、manual override 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on manus 'hand': manuscript is hand-written, manufacture is hand-made, manicure is hand-care, and manacle is a hand-ring.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 manus“手”上：manuscript 是手写，manufacture 是手做，manicure 是照料手，manacle 是套手的环。

items.meaning: by hand, by means of the hand
items.meaningCN: 用手地；手动地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The valve must be closed manually.
items.exampleCN: 这个阀门必须手动关闭。

items.meaning: the practice or doctrine of teaching deaf people by hand signs, or of emphasizing manual training
items.meaningCN: 手语教学法；强调手工训练的主张（-ism 构成做法或主义）
items.example: Manualism competed with oralism in deaf education.

items.meaning: a supporter of manual training or of hand-sign teaching

care for the hands and nails

definition_en: based on comparing two or more things, or measured in relation to something else
core_image: 两件东西放上同一台天平，一端翘起，一端下沉
scene: 老师把两位同学的作业并排放着讲评。 The comparative study showed clear differences between the two methods.
sceneCN: 这里 comparative 指「比较的」（第 1 个义项：以比较为基础的）；句意是这项比较研究显示两种方法之间有明显差异。

senses.title: Based on comparison
senses.definition: relating to or based on a comparison between things
senses.definitionCN: 与事物之间的比较有关的或以比较为基础的
senses.example: The team carried out a comparative study of two diets.
senses.exampleCN: 团队对两种饮食做了比较研究。
senses.why: The ending -ive marks an adjective that describes a way of looking at things.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 标志着一个形容词，用来描述一种观察事物的方式。

senses.title: Measured against something else
senses.definition: true only when measured against something else
senses.definitionCN: 只有与别的事物相对衡量时才成立
senses.example: The country enjoys a comparative advantage in cheap labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在廉价劳动力上有相对优势。
senses.why: What is large here may be small elsewhere, so the word keeps a sense of scale.
senses.whyCN: 此处的大在别处可能就小，所以这个词带着尺度感。

senses.title: The grammar form
senses.definition: the form of an adjective or adverb that compares two things
senses.definitionCN: 形容词或副词用于比较两者的形式
senses.example: Taller is the comparative of tall.
senses.exampleCN: taller 是 tall 的比较级。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for the form that sets two things side by side.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个词，指把两者并排的形式。

intro.en: Comparative comes from Latin comparativus, an adjective built on comparare, to set things side by side.
intro.cn: comparative 来自拉丁语 comparativus，这个形容词由 comparare（把事物并排放置）构成。

items.en: Comparare meant to set things side by side as equals.
items.cn: comparare 意为把事物作为同等者并排放置。

items.en: Comparativus described what belongs to comparison.
items.cn: comparativus 描述属于比较的东西。

items.en: Old French comparatif entered grammar talk.
items.cn: 古法语 comparatif 进入了语法讨论。

items.en: English comparative first described grammar forms.
items.cn: 英语 comparative 最初描述语法形式。

items.en: It now also labels studies that compare two systems.
items.cn: 如今它也用来标记比较两个体系的研究。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the other members of the compare family, and the meaning group names words for things judged in relation to others.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 compare 家族的其他成员，近义组列出表示相对衡量的词。

entries.definition: able to be compared
the act of comparing
to set things side by side
measured in relation to something else
showing differences between things
very different in a noticeable way

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a balance, then move to studies that compare and to the grammar form that sets two things side by side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从天平开始，再走到比较研究以及把两者并排的语法形式。

normal.en: Comparative keeps the idea of a balance: each side is read against the other.
normal.cn: comparative 保留了天平的意象：两边互相参照着读。

normal.en: A comparative study puts two cases in one frame.
normal.cn: 比较研究就是把两个案例放进同一个框架。

normal.en: Comparative advantage means you are better only relative to others.
normal.cn: 比较优势意味着你只是相对别人更强。

normal.en: In grammar, comparative is the middle step before the superlative.
normal.cn: 在语法里，比较级是最高级之前的中间一步。

normal.en: Comparatively is the adverb that softens a claim.
normal.cn: comparatively 是那个让说法变软的副词。

abstract.en: Picture two weights rocking a balance slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象两块砝码让天平缓缓摇摆。

abstract.en: Picture two reports spread open on one desk.
abstract.cn: 想象两份报告摊在同一张桌上。

abstract.en: Picture the word taller standing between tall and tallest.
abstract.cn: 想象 taller 站在 tall 与 tallest 之间。

examples.en: The book offers a comparative view of two legal systems.
examples.cn: 这本书对两种法律制度作了比较性的考察。

examples.en: In comparative terms, the second plan is cheaper.
examples.cn: 相对而言，第二个方案更便宜。

examples.en: Faster is the comparative of fast.
examples.cn: faster 是 fast 的比较级。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comparative 记成 compare（比较）加 ative：带着比较意味的，就是比较的、相对的。

root: 源自拉丁语 comparare（并列比较）与 comparativus，本义是属于比较的，后引申为相对的，并被语法借指比较级。

sensesIntro.en: From a method of study, to a way of measuring, and finally to a grammar form.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一种研究方法，到一种衡量方式，最后到一种语法形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two objects on one balance, one side rising as the other falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：两件东西放上同一台天平，一端翘起，一端下沉。

branches.en: The adjective first describes a method of study.
branches.cn: 这个形容词最初描述一种研究方法。

branches.en: Nothing is large in itself; it is large only in relation.
branches.cn: 没有什么本身就是大的，只有相对而言才大。

branches.en: Grammar takes the word for the form that weighs two things.
branches.cn: 语法借用这个词，指衡量两者的形式。

branches.en: A comparative study is also a study in relative worth.
branches.cn: 比较研究同时也是对相对价值的研究。

branches.en: Both judge one item against another.
branches.cn: 两者都是拿一项去对照另一项。

intro.en: Comparative adds the ending -ive to the base of compare, marking an adjective.
intro.cn: comparative 在 compare 的词基上加后缀 -ive，构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin comparare is the common source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 comparare 是这一整族词的共同来源。

items.example: The chart lists the comparatives of ten adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 图表列出了十个形容词的比较级。

items.example: Compared with last year, sales doubled.
items.exampleCN: 与去年相比，销量翻了一倍。

items.meaning: the act of setting side by side
items.exampleCN: 交换比较笔记对两队都有帮助。

items.example: The view is incomparable at sunset.
items.exampleCN: 日落时的景色无可比拟。

definition_en: the negative form of can, used to say that something is impossible or not allowed
core_image: 伸出去的手被一堵看不见的墙挡住
scene: 门锁着，钥匙也丢了，几个人只能站在门外。 The door was locked and the key was lost, so they cannot get in.
sceneCN: 这里 cannot 是「不能」（第 1 个义项：表示没有能力或条件做到）；句意是门锁着、钥匙也丢了，他们进不去。

derivatives.zh: cannot 的肯定形式，义为「能、可以」
语义对应的形容词，义为「不能的、无能力的」
语义对应的形容词，义为「无能力的、不能胜任的」

senses.title: To be unable to do something
senses.definition: used to say that someone or something is unable to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人或某物没有能力做到某事
senses.example: I cannot lift this box on my own.
senses.exampleCN: 我一个人抬不起这个箱子。
senses.why: cannot is simply can plus not: the word of ability carries the meaning and not reverses it.
senses.whyCN: cannot 就是 can 加 not：表示能力的词承担意义，not 把它翻转成否定。

senses.title: To be forbidden or impossible
senses.definition: used to say that something is not allowed or is impossible
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事不被允许或不可能发生
senses.example: You cannot park your car here.
senses.exampleCN: 你不能把车停在这里。
senses.why: English negation covers both inability and prohibition, so one form serves both uses.
senses.whyCN: 英语的否定既覆盖「做不到」，也覆盖「不许做」，所以同一个形式承担两种用法。

intro.en: cannot is not a borrowed word but a join: the old verb can fused with the negative not.
intro.cn: cannot 不是借来的词，而是拼接出来的：古老的动词 can 与否定词 not 合成一体。

items.en: cunnan meant to know or to know how, and it is the ancestor of modern can.
items.cn: cunnan 意为「知道、懂得」，是现代 can 的祖先。

items.en: The negative was written as two words, can not, with not coming from nāwiht, no thing.
items.cn: 否定形式写作两个词 can not，其中的 not 来自 nāwiht（无物）。

items.en: Printers joined the two words into cannot, and the single form spread through written English.
items.cn: 印刷商把两个词合成 cannot，这个单词形式在书面英语中传开。

items.en: The contraction can't became normal in speech, while cannot stayed the careful written form.
items.cn: 缩略形式 can't 在口语中成为常态，而 cannot 保持为正式的书面形式。

items.en: Today cannot is one word and covers both inability and prohibition.
items.cn: 今天 cannot 是一个词，同时表示「做不到」和「不许做」。

note.en: cannot is a fused form, so its look-alikes are the pieces it was made from and its contraction.
note.cn: cannot 是融合形式，所以形近词就是组成它的部件和它的缩略式。

entries.definition: the positive modal used for ability and permission
entries.definitionCN: 肯定形式的模态动词，表示能力或许可，是 cannot 的基础词。

entries.definition: the usual spoken contraction of cannot
entries.definitionCN: cannot 在口语中的常用缩略形式。

entries.definition: the word that makes a clause negative
entries.definitionCN: 使句子变成否定的否定词，是 cannot 的后半部分。

entries.definition: not able to do something
entries.definitionCN: 不能做到的，语义与「不能」相近。

entries.definition: lacking the ability or qualities needed
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏所需能力或素质的。

entries.definition: not able to happen or be done
entries.definitionCN: 不可能发生或做到的，对应「不可能」这一用法。

entries.definition: not allowed by a rule or law
entries.definitionCN: 被规则或法律禁止的，对应「不可以」这一用法。

normalIntro.en: There is nothing to decode here: cannot is can and not written as one word.
normalIntro.cn: 这里不需要拆解词根：cannot 就是把 can 和 not 写成一个词。

normal.en: can plus not gives the meaning directly: ability plus negation.
normal.cn: can 加 not 直接给出意义：能力加上否定。

normal.en: The form has no space, which marks it as the formal written choice.
normal.cn: 词中间没有空格，这使它成为正式的书面选择。

normal.en: Speech usually shortens it to can't, while writing keeps cannot.
normal.cn: 口语通常缩成 can't，书面语则保留 cannot。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as cannot help doing show the negation working inside a pattern.
normal.cn: cannot help doing 这类固定搭配展示了否定在句型里的作用。

normal.en: A bare verb follows it: cannot go, never cannot to go.
normal.cn: 它后面直接跟动词原形：cannot go，而不是 cannot to go。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for something and stopping against invisible glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸过去，却被看不见的玻璃挡住。

abstract.en: Picture a red light at a doorway, with your feet stopped at the line.
abstract.cn: 想象门口亮着红灯，脚步停在线外。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence with the words can do crossed out and rewritten as cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话里的「能做到」被划掉，改写成「做不到」。

examples.en: I cannot lift this box on my own.
examples.cn: 我一个人抬不起这个箱子。

examples.en: You cannot park your car here.
examples.cn: 你不能把车停在这里。

examples.en: She cannot come to the meeting tomorrow.
examples.cn: 她明天不能来参加会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看诺特」——门口挂着 no 的牌子，看见就知道不能进。

root: cannot 是 can 与 not 的合写：can 源自古英语 cunnan（知道、懂得），not 源自古英语 nāwiht（无物）。

sensesIntro.en: One negative form serves two jobs: a lack of ability and a rule that forbids.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个否定形式承担两项工作：能力上的不足，和规则上的禁止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stopped by an invisible wall just before it reaches the thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：手在快要够到东西时被一堵看不见的墙挡住。

branches.en: The plain inability sense: the strength or skill is not there.
branches.cn: 最基本的能力不足义：力气或技能不具备。

branches.en: The same negation applied to rules, where the block is a person or a law.
branches.cn: 同一个否定用在规则上，挡住你的是人或法律。

branches.en: Both senses share can plus not, and only the source of the block differs.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享 can 加 not 的结构，区别只在「阻挡者」不同。

branches.en: Public signs use cannot to state what visitors are not allowed to do.
branches.cn: 公共标识用 cannot 说明访客不许做什么。

branches.en: In writing, cannot signals a careful, formal register compared with can't.
branches.cn: 在书面语里，cannot 相比 can't 显得更谨慎、更正式。

intro.en: cannot is a compound of two native words rather than a prefixed or suffixed form.
intro.cn: cannot 是两个本族词的复合，而不是加前缀或后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic, so there is no Latin root to list for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 两个组成部分都属日耳曼语，因此这个词没有可列的拉丁词根。

items.example: They cannot agree on the date.
items.exampleCN: 他们就日期无法达成一致。

items.meaning: to be able to or be allowed to
the word that negates a clause

items.example: It is impossible to finish today.

definition_en: a person or company that pays for an event or supports someone

scene: 这家银行是比赛的赞助商。 The bank is a sponsor of the race.
sceneCN: 这里 sponsor 是「赞助商」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家银行是比赛的赞助商。

senses.title: A financial backer
senses.definition: a person or company that pays for an event
senses.definitionCN: 为活动出资的个人或公司
senses.example: The bank is a sponsor of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行是比赛的赞助商。
senses.why: Commercial backing is the most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 商业赞助是最常见的义项。

senses.title: One who proposes
senses.definition: a person who proposes or supports a plan or law
senses.definitionCN: 提出或支持计划、法律的人
senses.example: She was the sponsor of the new law.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这项新法律的发起人。
senses.why: Support begins with a formal proposal.
senses.whyCN: 支持始于正式的提议。

senses.title: To fund an event
senses.definition: to pay for or support an event or person
senses.definitionCN: 为活动或某人出资支持
senses.example: A local firm sponsors the team.
senses.exampleCN: 一家本地公司赞助这支球队。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of support.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示支持的动词。

intro.cn: sponsor 来自拉丁语 spondere，意为郑重承诺。

items.cn: spondere 意为郑重承诺。

items.en: Sponsor named a person who makes a promise.

items.cn: sponsor 指活动的资助者。

items.cn: 它又成为表示出资的动词。

note.en: Sponsor is compared with look-alike words and words for backers.
