definition_zh: 文明；文明社会；（某地某时期的）文化
definition_en: an advanced stage of human society with cities, writing and organised government, or the culture of a particular place and period
core_image: 河岸边升起的城墙、泥板文字与喧闹集市
scene: 博物馆的展柜里摆着泥板、青铜器和陶罐。 Writing marked the birth of civilization in the river valley.
sceneCN: 这里 civilization 指「文明」（第 1 个义项：拥有城市、文字与制度的社会阶段）；句意是文字的出现标志着河谷文明的诞生。

senses.title: An advanced human society
senses.definition: a society with cities, writing, industry and organised government
senses.definitionCN: 拥有城市、文字、手工业与有组织政府的社会
senses.example: Ancient civilizations grew up along great rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 古代文明在大河沿岸发展起来。
senses.why: Farm surpluses freed people to build cities and keep written records, and that whole package became the mark of a civilization.
senses.whyCN: 农业剩余让人腾出手来建城市、留文字记录，这一整套就成了文明的标志。

senses.title: The stage of social development
senses.definition: the stage of social development that such societies have reached
senses.definitionCN: 这类社会所达到的社会发展阶段
senses.example: Trade and writing pushed the region towards civilization.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易与文字把这一地区推向了文明。
senses.why: The same noun also names the achieved stage, an abstract level rather than one single society.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也指达到的阶段，是抽象层次而不是某个具体社会。

senses.title: The culture of a place or period
senses.definition: the way of life, art and ideas of a particular place or period
senses.definitionCN: 某一地方或时期的生活方式、艺术与观念
senses.example: The gallery traces the civilization of the Silk Road.
senses.exampleCN: 这座美术馆梳理了丝路沿线的文化。
senses.why: Because a society and its culture were seen as one whole, the word widened to mean a whole way of life.
senses.whyCN: 社会与文化被看作一个整体，于是这个词扩展为整套生活方式。

intro.en: Civilization grows from the Latin word for a citizen, not from a word for bricks or walls.
intro.cn: civilization 出自拉丁语里表示公民的词，而不是砖瓦城墙一类词。

items.en: Civis meant a citizen of a town.
items.cn: civis 指城邦或城镇的公民。

items.en: Civilis described anything belonging to citizens.
items.cn: civilis 形容属于公民的事物。

items.en: Civiliser meant to make a place fit for citizens.
items.cn: civiliser 指让一个地方变得适合公民居住。

items.en: Civilization first named the process, then the result.
items.cn: civilization 先指这个过程，后指结果。

items.en: The word now also covers the culture of a region.
items.cn: 这个词如今也涵盖一个地区的文化。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the civil family, while the meaning group names large human groupings.
note.cn: 形近组列出 civil 这一家族，近义组列出各类人群共同体。

entries.definition: relating to citizens or to ordinary people rather than the army or the church
entries.definitionCN: 与公民或普通人有关的，而非军队或教会的

entries.definition: a person who is not a member of the armed forces
entries.definitionCN: 不属于武装部队的平民

entries.definition: to bring a society to a more developed way of life
entries.definitionCN: 把一个社会带向更发达的生活方式

entries.definition: people living together in an organised community
entries.definitionCN: 在有组织的共同体中共同生活的人们

entries.definition: the customs, art and beliefs of a group of people
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体的习俗、艺术与信仰

entries.definition: a group of people who live in the same area or share an interest
entries.definitionCN: 住在同一地区或共享某种利益的一群人

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the citizen root, the city skyline, the written record and the culture sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从公民词根、城市天际线、文字记录与文化义入手。

normal.en: Civilization hides civis, the Latin word for a citizen, so the word begins with people, not with buildings.
normal.cn: civilization 里藏着拉丁语 civis（公民），所以这个词的起点是人，不是建筑。

normal.en: A civilization needs four things: a city, a script, a law and a surplus of food.
normal.cn: 一个文明需要四样东西：城市、文字、法律和余粮。

normal.en: The -ization ending marks a process, so the word names both the journey and the settled result.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ization 表示过程，因此这个词既能指历程也能指结果。

normal.en: Civilized describes people, while civilization describes the whole society.
normal.cn: civilized 形容人，civilization 形容整个社会。

normal.en: A clash of civilizations is a phrase from politics, not from archaeology.
normal.cn: a clash of civilizations 是政治学说法，不是考古学说法。

abstract.en: Picture a mud-brick wall rising beside a river, with a scribe counting grain behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象河边的土砖城墙升起，墙后有书吏在清点粮食。

abstract.en: Picture a clay tablet pressed with wedge marks, the first receipt in history.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被压出楔形痕迹的泥板，那是历史上第一张收据。

abstract.en: Picture a museum case holding a pot, a coin and a broken tablet.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆展柜里放着一只陶罐、一枚硬币和一块残破的泥板。

examples.en: The museum shows how civilization began in river valleys.
examples.cn: 博物馆展示了文明如何在河谷中起步。

examples.en: Every civilization leaves behind its tools, its laws and its stories.
examples.cn: 每个文明都会留下自己的工具、法律与故事。

examples.en: Scholars study the civilization of the Silk Road through its art.
examples.cn: 学者通过艺术品研究丝路沿线的文化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 civil 想成「市民的」，ization 想成「化」：市民聚居成城，就有了文明。

root: 源自拉丁语 civis（公民）与 civilis（公民的），经法语 civiliser 进入英语，本义是让一个地方适合公民聚居。

sensesIntro.en: From citizens to cities, then to a stage of development, and finally to a whole culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 从公民到城市，再到发展阶段，最后扩展到整套文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled town with a scribe and a market inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：带城墙的城镇，里面有书吏和集市。

branches.en: Cities, writing and law turn a settlement into a civilization.
branches.cn: 城市、文字与法律把聚落变成文明。

branches.en: The noun also names the stage a society has reached.
branches.cn: 这个名词也指一个社会达到的阶段。

branches.en: A society and its culture share the same word.
branches.cn: 社会与其文化共用一个词。

branches.en: The society and its level of development take one noun.
branches.cn: 社会与其发展水平用的是同一个名词。

branches.en: The culture branch keeps the everyday life of that society.
branches.cn: 文化分支保留了该社会的日常生活。

intro.en: One verb base grows a noun, two adjectives and a set of related civil words.
intro.cn: 一个动词词基长出名词、两个形容词以及一组 civil 相关词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin civis, a citizen, so every member of the family points back to town life.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 civis（公民），因此这一家族的每个成员都指向城镇生活。

items.meaning: to bring a society to a developed stage
items.example: Traders helped civilize the river ports.
items.exampleCN: 商人帮助河港走向文明。

items.meaning: having an advanced society or good manners
items.example: The city had a civilized air.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有一种文明的气息。

items.example: The railway had a civilizing effect on the coast.
items.exampleCN: 铁路对沿海产生了开化作用。

items.meaning: the advanced society or its stage
items.example: Writing is a mark of civilization.
items.exampleCN: 文字是文明的一个标志。

items.example: Old civilizations traded along the sea.
Civil law grew beside religious law.
items.exampleCN: 民法与宗教法并行发展。

items.meaning: a person outside the armed forces
items.example: The bridge was open to civilians.

latinEntries.example: Civis gave English the whole civil family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: civis 给了英语整个 civil 家族。

latinEntries.example: Civilis passed through French into English.

definition_zh: 湿的；潮湿的；弄湿；下雨的
definition_en: covered with water or another liquid, or full of moisture, either as a state or as an action
core_image: 刚洗完的头发贴在额头上，水珠一粒粒往下掉
scene: 跑进屋时头发全湿了，水顺着下巴滴到衣领上。 His coat was wet through after the long walk in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 wet 是「湿的」（第 1 个义项：表面被水或液体覆盖）；句意为在雨里走了很久，他的外套全湿透了。头发贴额、水珠往下滴的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Covered with liquid
senses.definition: covered or soaked with water or another liquid
senses.definitionCN: 被水或其他液体覆盖、浸透
senses.example: His coat was wet through after the long walk in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 在雨里走了很久，他的外套全湿透了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is physical water on a surface, and it still carries the strongest picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是表面的水，这一层至今仍是这个词最强烈的画面。

senses.title: Not yet dry
senses.definition: used of paint, ink or cement that has not yet hardened or dried
senses.definitionCN: 用于油漆、墨水或水泥尚未干硬的状态
senses.example: Mind the bench; the paint is still wet.
senses.exampleCN: 小心那条长椅，油漆还没干。
senses.why: Fresh liquid is still visible on the surface, so wet naturally describes work that is not finished.
senses.whyCN: 液体仍留在表面看得见，所以 wet 自然用来形容尚未完工的活儿。

senses.title: Rainy
senses.definition: used of weather or a season in which a lot of rain falls
senses.definitionCN: 形容天气或季节雨水很多
senses.example: It was the wettest summer the village had seen in years.
senses.exampleCN: 那是村里多年来雨水最多的一个夏天。
senses.why: Rainy weather leaves everything wet, so the adjective jumped from the surface to the sky that wets it.
senses.whyCN: 雨天会让一切变湿，于是这个形容词从被淋湿的表面跳到了使其淋湿的天空。

senses.title: To make something wet
senses.definition: to put water on something or let it become covered with liquid
senses.definitionCN: 把水弄到某物上，或让它被液体覆盖
senses.example: She wet a cloth and wiped the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她把布弄湿，擦了桌子。
senses.why: Any adjective in English can become a verb, and the verb simply names the act that produces the state.
senses.whyCN: 英语里形容词常可转作动词，这个动词只是给造成该状态的动作命名。

senses.title: In child talk, to lose urine
senses.definition: used about a child or an animal losing urine, or about the bed it happens in
senses.definitionCN: 用于幼儿或动物尿床、尿湿衣物
senses.example: The child wet the bed twice that week.
senses.exampleCN: 那星期孩子尿了两次床。
senses.why: The verb spread from wetting cloth to the liquid itself, and the bedroom gave it a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 动词从弄湿布料扩展到那液体本身，卧室里又给了它固定的说法。

intro.en: Wet comes from Old English wæt, the adjective for moist, and the related verb wætan meant to moisten; the family is shared across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: wet 源自古英语形容词 wæt（潮湿的），相关动词 wætan 意为使湿；这个词族在日耳曼语中通行。

items.en: The root meant water as well as the state of being watery, so noun and adjective grew from one seed.
items.cn: 这个词根既指水，也指含水的状态，名词与形容词由同一颗种子长出。

items.en: The adjective wæt described ground, weather and cloth, and the verb wætan was used for moistening food and clay.
items.cn: 形容词 wæt 描述地面、天气和布，动词 wætan 用于润湿食物与黏土。

items.en: The form settled as wet, and the doubled t in wetter and wettest became the usual spelling.
items.cn: 词形固定为 wet，比较级与最高级里的双 t 成为通行拼写。

items.en: Wet paint and wet through are fixed phrases that keep the surface picture alive in daily speech.
items.cn: wet paint 与 wet through 是固定短语，让表面的画面在日常口语中存活。

items.en: Science added wetland, and casual speech added a milder figurative use for soft opinions.
items.cn: 科学添上了 wetland（湿地），日常口语又给过于软弱的意见添了一层温和的比喻用法。

note.en: The first group gathers words whose shape or spelling is easily confused with wet, the second the words for moisture and rain.
note.cn: 第一组收外形与拼写容易与 wet 相混的词，第二组收表示潮湿与下雨的说法。

entries.definition: To sharpen a blade, or to stir an appetite, pronounced the same.
entries.definitionCN: 磨（刀）；刺激（胃口），与 wet 同音

entries.definition: A doctor for animals, or to examine carefully.
The past form of weep, to cry.
A net of threads, and the network of pages online.
Slightly wet, usually in an unpleasant way.
Slightly wet in a pleasant or wanted way.
Completely wet through, stronger than wet.
Of weather with much rain, a close match for the weather sense.

normalIntro.en: The word is short and heavy, like a cloth that holds water, and its family keeps the same three sounds.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词又短又沉，像一块吸了水的布，它的词族也保持同样的三个音。

normal.en: Wet and water share the same opening w, a shape like a wave.
normal.cn: wet 与 water 共享开头的 w，那是波浪的形状。

normal.en: Wetter has two t sounds, like two drips on a floor.
normal.cn: wetter 有两个 t 音，像地板上滴了两下。

normal.en: Whet sharpens a knife; wet soaks a cloth, so one letter decides blade or water.
normal.cn: whet 磨刀，wet 泡布，差一个字母就分出刀刃与水。

normal.en: Wetland is land that never quite dries, the word holding both halves.
normal.cn: wetland 是始终没干透的土地，这个词把两半都握住了。

normal.en: Wet paint signs exist because somebody will sit down.
normal.cn: 「油漆未干」的牌子之所以存在，是因为总有人会坐下。

abstract.en: Feel hair stuck to a forehead.
abstract.cn: 感觉头发贴在额头上。

abstract.en: Hear a drop hit a collar.
abstract.cn: 听见一滴水打上衣领。

abstract.en: See a footprint slowly filling with dark.
abstract.cn: 看一个脚印慢慢被深色填满。

examples.en: Take an umbrella, or you will get wet.
examples.cn: 带把伞吧，不然你会淋湿。

examples.en: Do not sit there; the paint is still wet.
examples.cn: 别坐那儿，油漆还没干。

examples.en: He wetted a cloth and cleaned the window.
examples.cn: 他把布弄湿，擦了窗户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂特」——喂，特先生，别站在雨里，你会湿透的。

root: 古英语 wæt（潮湿的）与 wætan（使湿）→ 中古英语 wet；同族有 water、wetness、wetland。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as water on a surface, stretches to paint and cement not yet dry, to rainy weather, to the act of making something wet, and finally to a child wetting the bed.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从表面的水开始，延伸到未干的油漆和水泥、多雨的天气、弄湿的动作，最后到孩子尿床。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of water sliding off a strand of hair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴水从一缕头发上滑落。

branches.en: The soaked branch: a coat wet through in the rain.
branches.cn: 浸湿分支：雨里湿透的外套。

branches.en: The unfinished-work branch: paint still wet on a bench.
branches.cn: 未完工分支：长椅上还没干的油漆。

branches.en: The weather branch: the wettest summer in years.
branches.cn: 天气分支：多年来最潮湿的夏天。

branches.en: The action branch: wetting a cloth to wipe a table.
branches.cn: 动作分支：弄湿布来擦桌子。

branches.en: The domestic branch: a child wetting the bed that week.
branches.cn: 家庭分支：孩子那星期尿床。

intro.en: Wet is a whole Old English adjective that also works as a verb, and its compounds are formed with -ness, -land and the -able ending.
intro.cn: wet 是完整的古英语形容词，也能直接作动词，其复合形式由 -ness、-land 和 -able 等词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source behind this word; the Latin entries below are only the borrowed scholarly words for the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁语来源；下面所列的拉丁条目只是同一概念借入英语的书面形式。

items.example: It also became a verb with no change.
items.exampleCN: 它原样不动地又成了动词。

definition_zh: 智力；机智；风趣；头脑；才子
definition_en: the power of thinking quickly and cleverly, and the ability to say amusing things
core_image: 对话里一句轻巧的反击落下，满桌人愣了一秒才同时笑出来
scene: 有人不客气地挑刺，他只用一句轻巧的反话回了过去，满桌人愣了一秒才笑出来。 Her wit made even boring meetings feel short.
sceneCN: 这里 wit 是「机智、风趣」（第 1 个义项：迅速而巧妙的思考与表达能力）；句意为她的风趣让连无聊的会议都觉得短。那句轻巧反击落下后全桌的笑声，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The power to think fast
senses.definition: the ability to think quickly and clearly, especially under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而清晰地思考的能力，尤其在压力之下
senses.example: He had the wit to see that the door was a trap.
senses.exampleCN: 他脑子够快，看出那扇门是个陷阱。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the mind itself, the seat of thought and sense.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是心智本身，是思想与知觉的所在。

senses.title: Clever and amusing speech
senses.definition: the talent for saying things that are clever and funny at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 把聪明与好笑合在一句话里的才能
senses.example: Her wit made even boring meetings feel short.
senses.exampleCN: 她的风趣让连无聊的会议都觉得短。
senses.why: When the quick mind comes out as speech, the same noun names the sparkle it produces.
senses.whyCN: 当敏捷的心变成言语，同一个名词就命名了它迸出的火花。

senses.title: A person of such talent
senses.definition: a clever and amusing person, used in older literary style
senses.definitionCN: 聪明而有风趣的人，多见于较旧的文体
senses.example: The party was full of wits and would-be poets.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会上满是有机锋的人和自封的诗人。
senses.why: The quality was used to name the people who carry it, a habit common in older English.
senses.whyCN: 这种品质被用来命名拥有它的人，这是老式英语中常见的习惯。

intro.en: Wit is Old English witt, the mind or understanding, from the same root as the verb witan, to know, which also gave wise.
intro.cn: wit 是古英语 witt（心智、理解），与动词 witan（知道）同根，而 wise 也出自这一族。

items.en: witt meant the mind and its power to understand, used in the plural for the senses.
items.cn: witt 指心智及其理解力，复数形式指五种感官。

items.en: The verb witan, to know, was one of the oldest and commonest verbs of thought.
items.cn: 动词 witan（知道）是最古老、最常见的思维动词之一。

items.en: The word moved from general mind to quick intelligence and to clever speech.
items.cn: 这个词从泛指的头脑移向敏捷的智力，再移向机智的言语。

items.en: The age of coffee houses and essays made wit the mark of a good talker.
items.cn: 咖啡馆与随笔的时代让 wit 成了健谈者的标志。

items.en: Wits keep the older sense of alertness, as in keeping your wits about you.
items.cn: 复数 wits 保留了警觉的旧义，如 keeping your wits about you。

note.en: The first group gathers words that resemble wit, the second other names for intelligence and humour.
note.cn: 第一组收与 wit 形近的词，第二组收表示智力与幽默的其他词。

entries.definition: To want something to happen.
Together, or by means of.
Clever and funny in speech.
The mind's alertness, in the plural.
The quality of being funny.
The power to learn and reason.
Lack of sense or quickness.

normalIntro.en: Wit is only three letters but holds two ideas: the mind and the joke it makes.
normalIntro.cn: wit 只有三个字母，却装了两个意思：头脑，和头脑开的玩笑。

normal.en: Put an h after w and you get whit, meaning a tiny bit, not the same word.
normal.cn: 在 w 后加 h 得到 whit，意为一点点，不是同一个词。

normal.en: Wit plus the -y ending gives witty: full of wit.
normal.cn: wit 加词尾 -y 得到 witty：满是机智。

normal.en: At your wits end is the picture of an empty box being shaken.
normal.cn: at your wits end 是一个空盒子被摇晃的画面。

normal.en: Wise and wit come from the same family: both are about knowing.
normal.cn: wise 与 wit 同族：都与知道有关。

normal.en: Outwit puts the smart one ahead of the other.
normal.cn: outwit 把聪明的那一方放到对方前面。

abstract.en: A short sentence, a half-second of silence, then laughter.
abstract.cn: 一句短话，半秒安静，然后是笑声。

abstract.en: A knife so thin that nobody feels it land.
abstract.cn: 一把薄刃，落下时没人察觉。

abstract.en: Two people looking at each other and both understanding at once.
abstract.cn: 两个人对视，同时明白。

examples.en: The old woman kept her wit sharp to the end.
examples.cn: 那位老妇人到晚年头脑依然敏锐。

examples.en: His reply showed real wit, and the room relaxed.
examples.cn: 他的回答显出真正的机智，屋里气氛一下松了。

examples.en: She was at her wits end with the leaking roof.
examples.cn: 面对漏水的屋顶，她已束手无策。

dict_mnemonic.text: wit 与 wise 同根，都表示「知道、明白」—— 脑子快的人，话也俏。

root: 古英语 witan（知道）→ witt（心智）→ 中古英语 wit；同族有 witty、outwit、wise。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the mind itself, then becomes the sparkle of clever speech, and finally names the person who talks that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从心智本身开始，成为聪明话语的火花，最后命名那样说话的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short reply followed by a whole table laughing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句短话之后，整桌人的笑。

branches.en: The mind branch: seeing that a door is a trap.
branches.cn: 心智分支：看出一扇门是陷阱。

branches.en: The speech branch: a meeting made short by humour.
branches.cn: 言语分支：被幽默缩短的会议。

branches.en: The person branch: a room full of wits.
branches.cn: 人物分支：满屋的才子。

branches.en: The spark branch: thought turning into a joke.
branches.cn: 火花分支：思考转成一个笑话。

branches.en: The portrait branch: a wit is someone whose talk is expected to amuse.
branches.cn: 画像分支：才子就是那个说话该让人发笑的人。

intro.en: Wit takes a few short endings and builds witty, witless and outwit; the plural wits is a noun of its own.
intro.cn: wit 接几个短词尾，构成 witty、witless、outwit；复数 wits 则是一个独立的名词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, so the Latin entries are borrowed words for intelligence and cleverness.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属于日耳曼语，所以拉丁条目是表示智力与机智的借入词。

items.example: The root turned into a mild insult.
items.exampleCN: 词根变成温和的骂人话。

definition_en: great pain or worry, a situation of serious danger, or to make someone suffer
core_image: 夜里电话铃突然响起，人从床上坐直，手心发凉
scene: 半夜铃声把他叫醒，听完一句话就坐在床沿发呆。 The ship sent a distress signal at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 distress 指「困境、危急」（第 2 个义项：处于危险而需要救援）；句意是那艘船在黎明时发出了求救信号。

senses.title: Great pain or worry
senses.definition: great pain, sorrow or worry of mind
senses.definitionCN: 心里极度的疼痛、悲伤或忧虑
senses.example: Her face showed real distress.
senses.exampleCN: 她脸上露出真正的痛苦。
senses.why: Pain that has nowhere to go settles in the whole body.
senses.whyCN: 无处可去的痛，会沉到整个身体里。

senses.title: Serious danger or need
senses.definition: a situation of great danger in which help is needed
senses.definitionCN: 处境危险而急需帮助
senses.example: The boat was in distress off the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘船在近海遇险。
senses.why: A call for help turns private pain into a public fact.
senses.whyCN: 一声呼救，把私人的痛变成众人皆知的事。

senses.title: To make someone suffer
senses.definition: to cause someone pain, sorrow or worry
senses.definitionCN: 使某人疼痛、悲伤或忧虑
senses.example: The news distressed the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让全家人都很痛苦。
senses.why: Sorrow crosses a room faster than any explanation.
senses.whyCN: 悲伤穿过一间屋，比任何解释都快。

intro.en: Distress comes from Latin distringere, to pull tight, from dis- and stringere, to draw or bind.
intro.cn: distress 来自拉丁语 distringere（拉紧），由 dis- 与 stringere（勒紧、捆绑）构成。

items.en: Stringere meant to draw tight or bind hard.
items.cn: stringere 指勒紧或紧紧捆住。

items.en: Dis- pulled the binding in opposite ways.
items.cn: dis- 把束缚往相反方向扯。

items.en: Distringere described being stretched and squeezed at once.
items.cn: distringere 描绘同时被拉扯与挤压。

items.en: Destresse named the tight, painful state.
items.cn: 古法语 destresse 指那种紧绷而痛苦的状态。

items.en: English used it for sorrow and for danger at sea.
items.cn: 英语借入后既指悲伤，也指海上的险情。

items.en: Today a signal, a debt and a loss can all bring distress.
items.cn: 今天求救信号、债务与失去都可能带来痛苦。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the stringere stem, while the meaning group gathers words for deep pain and hard times.
note.cn: 形近组共享 stringere 这段词干，近义组则聚起表示深痛与艰难的词。

entries.definition: pressure or worry under load
feeling under too much pressure
full of pain and worry
the state of going through pain
very severe mental pain
a life made hard by lack or trouble
entries.definitionCN: 因匮乏或困难而艰难的生活

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a phone ringing at night and end with a ship asking the shore for help.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从夜里响起的电话开始，落到一艘向岸边求救的船。

normal.en: Dis- plus stress: pressure pulled two ways becomes pain.
normal.cn: dis 加 stress，压力被两头一扯就成了痛苦。

normal.en: A letter from the bank threw her into distress.
normal.cn: 银行来的一封信让她陷入痛苦。

normal.en: The crew in distress fired a red light into the sky.
normal.cn: 遇险的船员朝天空放了一颗红色信号。

normal.en: The crying child distressed the whole carriage.
normal.cn: 哭着的孩子让整节车厢都不安。

normal.en: Debt can cause more distress than a bad day.
normal.cn: 债务带来的痛苦可能超过糟糕的一天。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled tight until the fibres start to part.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子被拉紧，纤维开始分离。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a phone at three in the morning.
abstract.cn: 想象凌晨三点，一只手按在电话上。

abstract.en: Picture a small boat sending one red light into the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小船向黑暗里放出一盏红灯。

examples.en: The letter caused her great distress.
examples.cn: 那封信让她非常痛苦。

examples.en: The crew was in distress near the rocks.
examples.cn: 船员在礁石附近遇险。

examples.en: The news distressed everyone at the table.
examples.cn: 这个消息让桌边所有人都很难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distress 记成「被拉紧的痛」：dis 表示分开，stress 与勒紧同源，绳子两头一扯，人就又痛又慌，也会让身边人跟着难受。

root: 源自拉丁语 distringere（拉紧），由 dis- 与 stringere（勒紧、捆绑）组成，经古法语 destresse 进入英语。本义是被拉扯、被挤压的紧绷状态，后来指心里的痛苦，也指海上等处的危急处境。

sensesIntro.en: From a rope pulled tight to a ship asking the shore for help in the dark.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一根被拉紧的绳子，到黑暗里向岸边求救的一艘船。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a phone ringing at night, and a body sitting up before the words arrive.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里电话响起，话还没听完，人已经从床上坐直。

branches.en: The first sense is the inner pain of being pulled tight.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是被拉紧之后心里的痛。

branches.en: The second sense is the outward danger that demands rescue.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是需要救援的外在险境。

branches.en: The third sense passes the pain to someone else.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把痛苦传到别人身上。

branches.en: Both senses move pain between people.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让痛苦在人与人之间移动。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs a signal and a rescuer.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要信号与救援者。

intro.en: Distress belongs to the stringere family, where Latin stringere, to draw tight, runs through stress and strict.
intro.cn: distress 属于 stringere 一族，拉丁语 stringere（拉紧）贯穿 stress 与 strict。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere, to draw tight, gives stress and strict; dis- and con- tighten it in different directions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere（拉紧）给出 stress 与 strict，前缀 dis- 与 con- 把紧绷推向不同方向。

items.meaning: to pull tight until it hurts
items.exampleCN: 这次失去带来深重的痛苦。

items.meaning: pressure put on a thing or a mind
items.example: Too much stress spoiled his sleep.
items.exampleCN: 压力太大毁了他的睡眠。

items.example: The school is strict about lateness.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校对迟到很严格。

items.example: The rules put a restriction on noise.

items.meaning: an area drawn off from the rest
items.example: The old district keeps its narrow lanes.
The rope strained under the weight.

definition_en: to look steadily at something for a long time, or a long steady look
core_image: 一个人久久望着夜空中的星星
scene: 她盯着星星看了几个小时。 She gazed at the stars for hours.
sceneCN: 这里 gaze 是「凝视」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她盯着星星看了几个小时。

senses.title: Look steadily
senses.definition: to look at something steadily for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 长时间稳定地看着某物
senses.example: She gazed at the stars for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她盯着星星看了几个小时。
senses.why: This is the core verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的动词义项。

senses.title: A steady look
senses.definition: a long, steady look at someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 长时间稳定地投向某人或某物的目光
senses.example: He held her gaze across the room.
senses.exampleCN: 隔着房间，他一直与她对视。
senses.why: The verb also names the look itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词也用来指目光本身。

senses.title: Look in wonder
senses.definition: to look with wonder or deep thought
senses.definitionCN: 带着惊叹或深思地看
senses.example: The child gazed into the shop window.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子出神地望着商店橱窗。
senses.why: Long looking often carries feeling.
senses.whyCN: 长久的观看常常带着情绪。

intro.en: Gaze appeared in Middle English, probably from a Scandinavian source.
intro.cn: gaze 在中古英语中出现，可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语。

items.en: A related northern word meant to stare or look.
items.cn: 一个相关的北方词语意为注视或看。

items.en: Gazen meant to look long and steadily.
items.cn: gazen 意为长久而稳定地看。

items.en: The verb settled in the form gaze.
items.cn: 这个动词固定为 gaze 的形式。

items.en: It also became a noun for a steady look.
items.cn: 它也成为名词，表示稳定的目光。

items.en: Writers gave it the sense of looking in wonder.
items.cn: 作家赋予它惊叹地观看的含义。

note.en: Gaze is compared with look-alike words and other verbs of looking.
note.cn: 把 gaze 与形近词以及其他表示看的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a very strong wind
a door in a fence or wall
a thin light cloth
to look directly for a long time
to look at something for a period of time
to look quickly at something

normalIntro.en: To gaze is to let the eyes rest on one thing.
normalIntro.cn: gaze 就是让目光停留在一样东西上。

normal.en: She gazed at the stars for hours.
normal.cn: 她盯着星星看了几个小时。

normal.en: He held her gaze across the room.
normal.cn: 隔着房间，他一直与她对视。

normal.en: The child gazed into the shop window.
normal.cn: 孩子出神地望着商店橱窗。

normal.en: They gazed at the sea in silence.
normal.cn: 他们默默地望着大海。

normal.en: She lowered her gaze and smiled.
normal.cn: 她垂下目光笑了。

abstract.en: A gaze is attention with nowhere else to go.
abstract.cn: 凝视是别无他处的注意力。

abstract.en: What we look at long enough begins to look back.
abstract.cn: 我们看久了的东西也开始回望我们。

abstract.en: Some questions are asked only with the eyes.
abstract.cn: 有些问题只用眼睛来问。

examples.en: She gazed at the stars for hours.
examples.cn: 她盯着星星看了几个小时。

examples.en: The child gazed into the shop window.
examples.cn: 孩子出神地望着商店橱窗。

examples.en: He held her gaze across the room.
examples.cn: 隔着房间，他一直与她对视。

dict_mnemonic.text: gaze 与 gate、gale 形近；gaze at 是「凝视」，meet someone's gaze 是「与某人对视」。

root: 中古英语 gazen（长久注视），可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语，核心义「目光停留在某处」。

sensesIntro.en: Gaze means to look steadily, the steady look itself, or to look in wonder.
sensesIntro.cn: gaze 意为稳定地看、那种稳定的目光，或出神地观看。

core.en: The eyes resting on one thing.
core.cn: 目光停留在一样东西上。

branches.en: The eyes stay on a distant star.
branches.cn: 目光停留在远处的星星上。

branches.en: Two people hold each other's look.
branches.cn: 两个人彼此接住对方的目光。

branches.en: A child stands lost before a window.
branches.cn: 孩子站在橱窗前出了神。

branches.en: The act of looking and the look itself share one word.
branches.cn: 看的动作与目光本身共用一个词。

branches.en: A long look can carry wonder or feeling.
branches.cn: 长久的注视可以带着惊叹或情感。

intro.en: Gaze builds words for people who look and for stargazing.
intro.cn: gaze 构成表示观看者和观星的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is probably Scandinavian in origin and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词可能源于斯堪的纳维亚语，没有拉丁语词根。

items.example: Do not gaze at the sun.
She gazes out of the window every morning.
items.exampleCN: 她每天早上都望着窗外。

items.example: He gazed at the painting for a long time.
She sat gazing at the fire.
The gazer stood still at the edge.
items.exampleCN: 凝视者一动不动地站在边缘。

items.meaning: a person who watches the stars
items.example: Stargazers met on the hill at night.
items.exampleCN: 观星者夜里在山丘上相聚。

items.example: They gazed at the empty road.
She answered with a steady gaze.

definition_en: having a large amount of money and possessions, or having plenty of something valuable
core_image: 一间储满粮食与布匹的库房，门一开就能看出屋主的家底
scene: 村口的宅子有石墙和两层楼，院子里停着两辆车。 The town grew wealthy on the wool trade in the sixteenth century.
sceneCN: 这里 wealthy 是「富有的」（第 1 个义项：拥有大量钱财与产业）；句意为这座城镇在十六世纪靠羊毛贸易富了起来。库房里堆满的粮食与布匹，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：富有的；富裕的；丰富的、大量的

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根名词，义为「财富；大量」
加副词后缀构成，义为「富足地；阔气地」
加名词后缀构成，义为「富裕」
与 well 相关的形近词，义为「福祉；幸福」

senses.title: Having much money
senses.titleCN: 富有的：拥有大量钱财与产业
senses.definition: having a great deal of money, property or other material goods
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量金钱、产业或其他物质财富
senses.example: The wealthy merchant owned four ships and half the dock.
senses.exampleCN: 这位富商拥有四条船和半个码头。
senses.why: Old English weal means well-being, and wealth was originally that whole state; money became its measure.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 weal 意为「安好」，wealth 本指整个好境况；金钱后来成了它的度量。

senses.title: As a group
senses.titleCN: 富人：作为一个群体来看的富有者
senses.definition: in the phrase the wealthy, the whole group of rich people
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the wealthy，指全部富人这一群体
senses.example: The tax falls hardest on the wealthy and lightest on the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税对富人最重，对穷人最轻。
senses.why: Adjectives preceded by the can name a class, so the rich quality turns into the people who have it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词前加 the 可以指一类人，于是「富」这一性质变成了拥有它的人群。

senses.title: Rich in natural goods
senses.titleCN: 资源丰富的：物产或条件富足
senses.definition: rich in natural resources, land or production
senses.definitionCN: 在自然资源、土地或产出方面富足
senses.example: The valley is wealthy in water, which the plains below lack.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷水源丰富，而下面的平原却缺水。
senses.why: The abundance that money measures also exists in land: the word follows the goods, not the bank account.
senses.whyCN: 金钱所衡量的那种充足也存在于土地中：这个词跟的是物产，而不是银行户头。

senses.title: Rich in a quality
senses.titleCN: 丰富的：在某种特质上含量多
senses.definition: having a large amount of a particular quality or element, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某种品质或成分含量很多
senses.example: The region is wealthy in stories, and every village tells them differently.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带故事极多，每个村庄讲得都不一样。
senses.why: Once plenty is the meaning, anything countable can be the treasure that fills the storehouse.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「充足」成了核心义，任何可数的东西都能成为填满库房的宝藏。

senses.title: Prosperous in life
senses.definition: enjoying a comfortable and prosperous way of life, without the stress on huge sums
senses.definitionCN: 生活舒适宽裕，不特别强调数目巨大
senses.example: After two good harvests the farmhouse looked wealthy again.
senses.exampleCN: 连收两季好庄稼之后，那座农舍又显得富足了。
senses.why: This is the old well-being again, visible in a house rather than counted in coins.
senses.whyCN: 这又回到了古老的「安好」，它显在一座房子里，而不是数在铜板中。

intro.en: Wealthy grows from wealth, whose oldest sense was not money but well-being.
intro.cn: wealthy 由 wealth 生长而来，而 wealth 最初的意思不是钱，而是「安好」。

items.en: Weal meant 'well-being, welfare, prosperity', the same element as in commonweal.
items.cn: weal 意为「安好、福祉、兴旺」，与 commonweal 中的成分相同。

items.en: Wela meant 'wealth, riches', and the two words were closely associated.
items.cn: wela 意为「财富、财宝」，两者关系密切。

items.en: Wele or welthe came to name both prosperity and the things that show it.
items.cn: 中古英语 wele 与 welthe 既指兴旺，也指显出兴旺的那些东西。

items.en: The suffix -y forms the adjective, and wealthy appears alongside the older wele. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 构成形容词 wealthy，它与更早的 wele 并存；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense narrowed toward money and property, while the figurative sense of abundance survived.
items.cn: 词义向金钱与财产收窄，而表示「丰富」的比喻义照旧留存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wealth family; the near-meaning group gathers words for being rich.
note.cn: 形近组收 wealth 一族词；近义组收表示富有的词。

entries.definition: Riches, or a large amount of something good.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财富」，或指某物的「大量」。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for the state of being wealthy; rare in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「富裕」，口语中罕见。

entries.definition: The state of being well in body; a shared shape, different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「健康」，与 wealthy 形近而义不同。

entries.definition: A political community; keeps the old weal of well-being.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「联邦、共同体」，保留了 weal「福祉」的旧义。

entries.definition: Having much money or many resources; the commonest word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富的」，是最常用的说法。

entries.definition: Prosperous and well-off; formal and often about societies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富裕的」，语气正式，多用于社会群体。

entries.definition: Comfortably provided for, without implying great riches.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽裕的」，不含巨富之意。

entries.definition: Thriving and successful, often of a business or a town.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴旺的」，多形容事业或城镇。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English weal and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 weal，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: wealth began as well-being, and only later counted money.
normal.cn: wealth 起初指安好，后来才开始数钱。

normal.en: Wealthy adds -y to wealth, just as healthy adds -y to health.
normal.cn: wealthy 由 wealth 加 -y，正如 healthy 由 health 加 -y。

normal.en: The wealthy means all rich people together, not one rich person.
normal.cn: the wealthy 指全部富人，不是某一位富人。

normal.en: A region can be wealthy in water or in stories, not only in cash.
normal.cn: 一个地区可以水富、故事富，不只是钱富。

normal.en: Well-off is milder than wealthy; it stops short of great riches.
normal.cn: well-off 比 wealthy 温和，不含巨富之意。

abstract.en: Picture a storehouse packed with grain and cloth: the wealth shows in what can be drawn on.
abstract.cn: 想象一间堆满粮食与布匹的库房：财富显现在可取用的东西上。

abstract.en: The word measures plenty, so it can point at money, water, or a store of tales.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量的是「充足」，所以能指向金钱、水，或一大堆故事。

abstract.en: Its oldest layer is not greed but welfare: to be wealthy once meant to be well.
abstract.cn: 它最古老的一层不是贪婪而是福祉：有钱曾经意味着过得好。

examples.en: The wealthy family owned most of the land in the valley.
examples.cn: 那个富裕家族拥有谷中大部分土地。

examples.en: The country is wealthy in forests but poor in oil.
examples.cn: 这个国家森林丰富，却缺乏石油。

examples.en: The shop moved to a wealthier district last spring.
examples.cn: 这家店去年春天搬到了更富裕的街区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威（weal）尔西（thy）」——威尔西家库房里粮布堆到屋顶：富有的

root: 由中古英语 welthe「兴旺、财富」加形容词后缀 -y 构成，更早来自古英语 weal「福祉」与 wela「财富」；同族词有 wealth、commonwealth。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wealthy run from cash and property to the class of rich people, then to abundance of resources, of qualities, and of a comfortable life.
sensesIntro.cn: wealthy 的五个义项从钱财产业出发，到富人这一群体，再到资源充足、品质丰富，以及生活宽裕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storehouse packed with grain and cloth, its wealth plain as soon as the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间堆满粮食布匹的库房，门一开就看得出家底。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: cash, property and a comfortable life.
branches.cn: 金钱线：现金、产业与宽裕的生活。

branches.en: CLASS LINE: the adjective becomes a name for rich people.
branches.cn: 群体线：形容词成了富人的称呼。

branches.en: PLENTY LINE: water, forests or stories in abundance.
branches.cn: 充足线：水、森林或故事方面的丰富。

branches.en: ROOT LINE: the old sense of well-being still glows under the money.
branches.cn: 词根线：金钱之下还隐约闪着古老的「安好」义。

branches.en: CONTRAST: rich is plainer, affluent more formal.
branches.cn: 对照线：rich 更朴素，affluent 更正式。

intro.en: Wealthy is a native noun plus the common adjective suffix -y.
intro.cn: wealthy 是本族名词加常见形容词后缀 -y 构成的。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_en: to make someone believe something that is not true
core_image: 一只手在桌下悄悄换掉了牌
scene: 他嘴上说得漂亮，背后却换掉了账本。 She did not mean to deceive anyone.
sceneCN: 这里 deceive 指「欺骗」（第 1 个义项：让人相信假的事）；句意是她并非有意骗人。

senses.title: Make someone believe a lie
senses.definition: to cause a person to accept something false as true
senses.definitionCN: 让一个人把假的当成真的接受下来
senses.example: She did not mean to deceive anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她并不是有意骗谁。
senses.why: A lie only works when another mind takes it in.
senses.whyCN: 谎言只有在另一个脑子接收之后才算成立。

senses.title: Trick someone into acting
senses.definition: to lead a person by false words into doing something
senses.definitionCN: 用假话把某人引去做某件事
senses.example: He deceived the old man into signing the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他骗老人签了那份文件。
senses.why: False words become a handle that turns another hand.
senses.whyCN: 假话成了一个把手，能转动别人的手。

senses.title: Cheat the eye
senses.definition: to give the senses a false impression
senses.definitionCN: 给感官一个不真实的印象
senses.example: The mirror deceives the eye and makes the room look wider.
senses.exampleCN: 镜子骗过眼睛，让房间显得更宽。
senses.why: What looks true can be built on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 看上去真的东西，也可能是特意做出来的。

intro.en: Deceive came from Old French deceivre, from Latin decipere, to catch in a trap, built on capere, to take.
intro.cn: deceive 来自古法语 deceivre，源于拉丁语 decipere（设套捕捉），根子是 capere（拿取）。

items.en: Decipere meant to catch something in a trap.
items.cn: decipere 指用套子把东西捉住。

items.en: The trap became a trick played on a person's mind.
items.cn: 网套变成了设在人心上的圈套。

items.en: Deceivre carried the sense of betraying trust.
items.cn: deceivre 带着背弃信任的意味。

items.en: Deceive entered English as both cheat and mislead.
items.cn: deceive 进入英语时兼指行骗与误导。

items.en: Deceive is now mostly about beliefs rather than property.
items.cn: 如今 deceive 多指骗人的认知，而不只是骗财物。

note.en: The look-alike group all end in the same sound, and the meaning group moves from small tricks to large fraud.
note.cn: 形近组收着同一个尾音，近义组则从小花招走到大诈骗。

entries.definition: to get something that is given or sent
entries.definitionCN: 收到别人给或寄来的东西

entries.definition: to form an idea in the mind
to notice or understand something
to act dishonestly to win or gain
entries.definitionCN: 为取胜或得利而做不诚实的事

entries.definition: to guide someone to a wrong belief
to fool someone for fun or gain
entries.definitionCN: 为了好玩或得利而捉弄人

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a card swapped under a table and end with a mirror that lies about the room.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌下被换掉的一张牌开始，落到一面谎报房间大小的镜子。

normal.en: A lie needs two people: one to speak it, one to believe it.
normal.cn: 谎言需要两个人：一个说，一个信。

normal.en: The surest liar first makes you trust him.
normal.cn: 最稳的骗子，先让你信任他。

normal.en: Nobody likes being deceived; everybody has deceived himself.
normal.cn: 没人喜欢被骗，可每个人都骗过自己。

normal.en: The eye is easiest to fool because it never asks questions.
normal.cn: 眼睛最容易骗，因为它从不提问。

normal.en: De- away, -ceive take: to be deceived is to be taken aside.
normal.cn: de 是离开，ceive 是拿取，被骗就是被人悄悄拿走。

abstract.en: Picture a hand under the table moving one card.
abstract.cn: 想象桌下一只手挪动了一张牌。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that is prepared before the question is asked.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在问题提出之前就准备好的微笑。

abstract.en: Picture a painted door that opens onto a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇画上去的门，推开却是墙。

examples.en: She did not mean to deceive anyone.
examples.cn: 她并不是有意骗谁。

examples.en: The advertisement deceived buyers about the size of the flat.
examples.cn: 广告在房子面积上骗了买家。

examples.en: Do not deceive yourself that the work is finished.
examples.cn: 别自欺欺人地以为活儿已经干完了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deceive 记成「递西服」：de 是递，ceive 像收，把一件假西服递过去让人收下，就是骗人。

root: 经古法语 deceivre 进入英语，源于拉丁语 decipere，本义是「设套捉住」，由 de（离开）与 capere（抓取）构成。捕兽的网套后来变成设在人心上的骗局，所以这个词从一开始就带着「套住」的意味。

sensesIntro.en: From making a mind accept a falsehood, to leading a hand into an act, to fooling the eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让一个脑子接受假话，到把一只手引进某个动作，再到骗过眼睛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card swapped under the table while faces stay calm.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌下换掉一张牌，桌上的表情不变。

branches.en: The first sense is the false belief planted in another mind.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是种进别人脑子里的错误相信。

branches.en: The belief is then used to move the deceived person into action.
branches.cn: 这份相信随后被用来推动受骗的人去做事。

branches.en: The senses can be fooled without any belief at all.
branches.cn: 感官可以在没有任何相信的情况下被蒙住。

branches.en: False words first enter the mind, then leave it as a deed.
branches.cn: 假话先进脑子，再以行动的形式离开它。

branches.en: Both senses describe a false picture that produces a real result.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说假画面造出了真结果。

intro.en: Deceive gathers its whole family: the act, the quality, the person, and the plainer noun deceit.
intro.cn: deceive 把整族都聚齐了：行为、性质、行骗的人，还有更朴素的 deceit。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is capere, to take or seize, with de- adding the sense of away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 capere（抓取），前缀 de- 添上「拿走」的意味。

items.meaning: to make someone believe a lie

items.exampleCN: 那个骗子始终没被抓住。

items.example: He felt deceived by the letter.
items.exampleCN: 那封信让他觉得受了骗。

items.example: The contract was signed by deceit.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同是靠欺诈签下的。
这项任务看着简单，其实不然。

latinEntries.example: Capere gives English capture, receive and deceive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capere 给英语带来 capture、receive 和 deceive。

definition_en: something that takes your attention away from what you are doing, or a pleasant way to pass the time
core_image: 书页边上晃过一只飞蛾，眼睛跟着它走了半行
scene: 台灯下刚写两行，窗玻璃上扑来一只飞蛾。 The phone on the desk is a constant distraction.
sceneCN: 这里 distraction 指「让人分心的事物」（第 1 个义项：把注意力拉走的东西）；句意是桌上那部手机总让人分心。

senses.title: Something that pulls the mind away
senses.definition: a thing or person that takes your attention from what you are doing
senses.definitionCN: 把你注意力从手头事情上拉走的东西或人
senses.example: Loud music is a distraction when I study.
senses.exampleCN: 我学习时大声的音乐就是一种干扰。
senses.why: Attention is a single thread, and any hand can tug it.
senses.whyCN: 注意力只有一根线，谁伸手都能拽一下。

senses.title: A pleasant way to pass time
senses.definition: an activity that keeps the mind amused or calm
senses.definitionCN: 让心思得到消遣或安静下来的活动
senses.example: The market was a happy distraction for the children.
senses.exampleCN: 集市对孩子们来说是个开心的消遣。
senses.why: The same pulling hand is welcome when the task is dull.
senses.whyCN: 事情枯燥时，那只拉走注意力的手反倒受欢迎。

intro.en: Distraction comes from Latin distrahere, to pull apart, from dis-, apart, and trahere, to draw.
intro.cn: distraction 来自拉丁语 distrahere（拉开），由 dis-（分开）与 trahere（拉）构成。

items.en: Trahere meant to draw or drag something along.
items.cn: trahere 指拉动或拖着东西走。

items.en: Dis- pulled the mind in more than one direction.
items.cn: dis- 把心思往好几个方向拉。

items.en: Distractio named the state of being pulled apart.
items.cn: distractio 指被拉散的状态。

items.en: English used it for a mind torn between things.
items.cn: 英语借入时指心思被扯成几块。

items.en: The milder sense of amusement took hold.
items.cn: 后来较温和的「消遣」义站稳了脚。

items.en: A screen, a sound and a worry are all distractions today.
items.cn: 今天的屏幕、声响与心事都算分心之物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trahere stem, while the meaning group lists other breaks in attention.
note.cn: 形近组共享 trahere 这段词干，近义组则是几种打断注意力的情形。

entries.definition: to pull attention away
unable to keep the mind on one thing
entries.definitionCN: 无法把心思集中在一处

entries.definition: likely to pull attention away
something that breaks the quiet
a sudden break in what is happening
entries.definitionCN: 正在进行之事被突然打断

entries.definition: a gentle way to pass the time

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a moth on the window and end with a dull afternoon made lighter.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从窗上的一只飞蛾开始，落到一个被照亮一点的沉闷下午。

normal.en: Dis- plus tract: the mind is pulled apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 tract，心思就被往两边拉开。

normal.en: A single message can be a distraction for a whole hour.
normal.cn: 一条消息就能让人分心整整一小时。

normal.en: Turn the phone face down and the distraction goes quiet.
normal.cn: 把手机扣过去，分心之物就安静了。

normal.en: The market gave the children a welcome distraction.
normal.cn: 集市给了孩子们一段愉快的消遣。

normal.en: Too many distractions make a short task long.
normal.cn: 分心的事一多，短活也拖成长活。

abstract.en: Picture a moth crossing the page while the eyes follow it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只飞蛾掠过纸面，眼睛跟着它走。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tugging one thread out of a neat row.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从整齐的一排里抽走一根线。

abstract.en: Picture a noisy room fading when a favourite song starts.
abstract.cn: 想象喜爱的歌一起，吵闹的房间就退远了。

examples.en: The noise outside was a constant distraction.
examples.cn: 外面的噪声让人一直分心。

examples.en: She worked for an hour without distractions.
examples.cn: 她心无旁骛地工作了一个小时。

examples.en: A walk in the park offered a welcome distraction.
examples.cn: 去公园走走成了一段愉快的消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distraction 记成「被拉走的心思」：dis 表示分开，tract 表示拉，心思被往旁边一拉，就有了让人分心的事，也可能是一段消遣。

root: 源自拉丁语 distrahere（拉开），由 dis-（分开）与 trahere（拉）组成。本义是把人的心思往不同方向拉扯，因此指打断注意力的东西；当拉扯来自愉快之事时，又引申为消遣与解闷。

sensesIntro.en: From a moth crossing the page to a dull hour made lighter by something pleasant.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只飞蛾掠过纸面，到一段因愉快之事而变轻的沉闷时光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a moth crossing the page while the eyes follow it away from the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只飞蛾掠过纸面，眼睛跟着它离开原来那一行。

branches.en: The first sense is any pull that steals attention.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是任何偷走注意力的拉扯。

branches.en: The second sense is a pull that is welcome.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是受欢迎的拉扯。

branches.en: Both senses move the mind off its present task.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把心思从眼前的事上移开。

branches.en: Both are judged by what the mind leaves behind.
branches.cn: 两个义项都看心思离开了什么来评判。

branches.en: Only the second sense leaves a pleasant memory.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项留下愉快的记忆。

intro.en: Distraction sits in the trahere family, where Latin trahere, to draw, meets several prefixes.
intro.cn: distraction 属于 trahere 一族，中心是拉丁语 trahere（拉），前后接上不同前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere, to draw, gives distraction, attract and extract; the prefix decides which way the pull goes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere（拉）给出 distraction、attract 与 extract，前缀决定往哪个方向拉。

items.example: The phone is a constant distraction.

items.meaning: the grip of a wheel on a surface
items.example: The tyres lost traction on ice.
items.exampleCN: 轮胎在冰上失去抓地力。

definition_en: used to add another point, or in an extra way
core_image: 一篇报告的末尾又补上一段「还有一点」
scene: 票价之外，乘客还要为行李另外付费。 Additionally, passengers pay for their luggage.
sceneCN: 这里的 Additionally 是「此外」（第 1 个义项：引出补充的一点）；句中在票价之外再补一项费用。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly，义为「额外的」
同源名词，义为「添加；加法」
同源基础动词，义为「添加」

senses.title: Here is one more point
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to add a further point
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，引出另一条补充的信息
senses.example: Additionally, the museum closes on Mondays.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，博物馆每周一闭馆。
senses.why: The adverb of additional marks a point joined to the list already given, so it works as a connector.
senses.whyCN: additional 的副词表示「又并进一条」，所以它天然充当连接词。

senses.title: In an extra way
senses.definition: in a way that is charged or supplied on top of the usual amount
senses.definitionCN: 以在通常数额之外另行收取或提供的方式
senses.example: The room was additionally charged for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 这间房的早餐是额外收费的。
senses.why: In this use the adverb modifies the verb rather than linking sentences, so it describes how the charge is made.
senses.whyCN: 这种用法里副词修饰的是动词而不是连接句子，描述的是「以何种方式收费」。

intro.en: The adverb is additional plus the ordinary ly ending, a late formation.
intro.cn: 这个副词由 additional 加常见的 ly 词尾构成，出现得较晚。

items.en: addere meant to give to, hence to add.
items.cn: addere 意为给到……上，因此引申为添加。

items.en: additio named the act of adding.
items.cn: additio 指添加这一行为。

items.en: additional was formed from addition.
items.cn: additional 由 addition 派生。

items.en: additionally appeared as a written connector.
items.cn: additionally 作为书面连接词出现。

items.en: it is now common in reports, contracts and formal writing.
items.cn: 如今它常见于报告、合同与正式文书。

note.en: The first group shares the add stem; the second gives other linking adverbs.
note.cn: 第一组共享 add 词干；第二组是别的连接副词。

entries.definition: extra
the act of adding
to put something in
something added to food
and in addition
in addition to that
apart from that
as well

normalIntro.en: additional plus ly: the connector that says there is one more thing.
normalIntro.cn: additional 加 ly：那句「还有一点」的连接词。

normal.en: Use a comma after it when it opens a sentence.
normal.cn: 放在句首时要加逗号。

normal.en: It is more formal than also or besides.
normal.cn: 它比 also、besides 更正式。

normal.en: It never joins two clauses without a full stop.
normal.cn: 它不能在没有句号的情况下直接连接两个分句。

normal.en: The adjective is additional; do not drop the ly in the adverb.
normal.cn: 形容词是 additional，副词别漏掉 ly。

normal.en: One l in the middle, one l at the end: additio-nally.
normal.cn: 中间一个 l，末尾还有 l：additio-nally。

abstract.en: See a report with a short final paragraph marked one more point.
abstract.cn: 想象报告末尾多出一小段「还有一点」。

abstract.en: Picture a bill with a second column of charges.
abstract.cn: 想象账单上多出第二列收费。

abstract.en: Think of a speaker raising one finger after saying last.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者说完「最后」又竖起一根手指。

examples.en: Additionally, the office will close an hour early.
examples.cn: 此外，办公室会提前一小时关门。

examples.en: The service is additionally charged at ten percent.
examples.cn: 这项服务另外收取百分之十的费用。

examples.en: Additionally, all visitors must show an identity card.
examples.cn: 另外，所有访客都必须出示身份证件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪申诺里」——阿迪申报完了，诺里又在后面补了一句「另外」。

root: 由 additional（额外的）加副词词尾 -ly 构成，additional 又出自 addition 与拉丁语 addere（加到……上）；核心是「在已有的话之外再补一条」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb links sentences, and one modifies how something is charged.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词，一种连接句子，一种修饰收费的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a last paragraph that says one more thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：末尾那段「还有一点」。

branches.en: a further point added to a list
branches.cn: 在清单上再加一条

branches.en: an amount charged on top
branches.cn: 另外加收的数额

branches.en: the written link between two statements
branches.cn: 两句之间的书面连接

branches.en: the manner of an extra charge
branches.cn: 额外收费的方式

branches.en: adding words and adding costs
branches.cn: 加话与加钱

intro.en: The adjective of addition takes the standard adverb ending.
intro.cn: addition 的形容词接上标准副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root addere also gives add, addition and additive.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 addere 还给出 add、addition 与 additive。

definition_en: a small carpet for a floor; a thick blanket; an informal word for a hairpiece
core_image: 一块铺在地上、质地厚实的织物
scene: 她床边铺着一块小小的羊毛地毯。 A small wool rug lay beside her bed.
sceneCN: 这里 rug 是「小地毯」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她床边铺着一块小小的羊毛地毯。

senses.title: Small carpet
senses.definition: a small carpet used on a floor
senses.definitionCN: 铺在地上的小块地毯
senses.example: She laid a rug by the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她在床边铺了一块小地毯。
senses.why: The core object is a small floor covering.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是铺地的小块织物。

senses.title: Thick blanket
senses.definition: a thick blanket used for warmth
senses.definitionCN: 用来保暖的厚毯
senses.example: He wrapped a wool rug around his shoulders.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一条羊毛厚毯披在肩上。
senses.why: The same coarse fabric serves as a wrap.
senses.whyCN: 同样的粗织物也可当披盖。

senses.title: Hairpiece
senses.definition: an informal word for a hairpiece
senses.definitionCN: 假发的非正式说法
senses.example: Everyone noticed his new rug.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都注意到了他的新假发。
senses.why: A covering on a surface becomes a covering on the head.
senses.whyCN: 覆在表面的东西变成覆在头上的东西。

intro.en: Rug probably comes from a Scandinavian word for a coarse cover.
intro.cn: rug 可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语中表示粗毯的词。

items.en: Rugga names a rough, shaggy cover.
items.cn: rugga 指粗糙、毛茸茸的覆盖物。

items.en: Rugge means a coarse woollen cloth.
items.cn: rugge 意为粗毛织物。

items.en: Rug narrows to a floor covering.
items.cn: rug 收窄为铺地织物。

items.en: Rug also means a warm travelling blanket.
items.cn: rug 也指旅行用的保暖毯。

items.en: Rug gains the slang sense of a hairpiece.
items.cn: rug 获得「假发」的俚语义。

note.en: A rug covers the floor; a rag is a torn cloth.
note.cn: rug 铺在地上，rag 则是破布。

normalIntro.en: A rug is a thick cover, usually on the floor.
normalIntro.cn: rug 是一块厚实的覆盖物，通常铺在地上。

normal.en: A red rug warmed the cold room.
normal.cn: 一块红地毯让冷屋子暖和起来。

normal.en: She shook the dust from the rug.
normal.cn: 她抖掉小地毯上的灰尘。

normal.en: He sat on a rug in front of the fire.
normal.cn: 他坐在炉火前的地毯上。

normal.en: The cat slept on the kitchen rug.
normal.cn: 猫睡在厨房的小地毯上。

normal.en: They spread a rug under the tree.
normal.cn: 他们在树下铺开一块毯子。

abstract.en: Picture a bright square warming a bare floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一块明亮的小方毯温暖光秃的地面。

abstract.en: Imagine coarse wool woven into a soft cover.
abstract.cn: 想象粗羊毛被织成柔软的覆盖物。

abstract.en: Think of a traveller wrapped against the cold.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人裹着毯子御寒。

examples.en: The rug in the hall is faded and worn.
examples.cn: 门厅里的地毯已经褪色磨损。

examples.en: He spread a rug on the grass for lunch.
examples.cn: 他在草地上铺了块毯子吃午饭。

examples.en: We bought a small rug for the bathroom.
examples.cn: 我们给浴室买了一块小地毯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rug」短促有力，像一块被铺平、踩在脚下的厚毯。

root: 可能源自斯堪的纳维亚语 rugga（粗毛覆盖物），经中古英语 rugge（粗毛织物）演变为「小地毯」。

sensesIntro.en: Rug means a small floor carpet, a thick blanket, or informally a hairpiece.
sensesIntro.cn: rug 意为小地毯、厚毯，或俚语中的假发。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick woven square on a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：铺在表面上的一块厚织物。

branches.en: The main sense is a small floor carpet.
branches.cn: 主要义是铺地的小地毯。

branches.en: The covering serves as a warm blanket.
branches.cn: 这种覆盖物也可当保暖毯。

branches.en: The idea of a cover extends to a hairpiece.
branches.cn: 「覆盖物」的概念扩展到假发。

branches.en: Both are thick woven covers people use.
branches.cn: 两者都是人们使用的厚织覆盖物。

branches.en: Floor cover and head cover share the shape idea.
branches.cn: 地面覆盖与头部覆盖共享「盖住」的概念。

intro.en: Rug is a short old word with compound partners.
intro.cn: rug 是个古老的短词，常与其他词构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Rug has no Latin root; it is of Scandinavian origin.
latinIntro.cn: rug 没有拉丁词根，源自斯堪的纳维亚语。

items.example: Rugge is an early English form.
